issues.title: Remote links on issues
issues.body:
## User story

As an Armature user, I want to see which external documentation pages reference an issue, so that I can jump from the work item to its spec. The first consumer is Stator (praetorianer777/Stator#32).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `issue_remote_link` (org, issue, url, title, source application, icon url, created by, created at) with the usual tenant-isolation RLS policy; unique on (issue, url)
- [ ] `GET/POST /api/v1/issues/{issueKey}/remote-links` and `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{issueKey}/remote-links/{id}`, in the route table, so they appear in `api/openapi.json` and as MCP tools
- [ ] POST with an existing URL updates the title instead of duplicating (idempotent sync)
- [ ] Only users who can edit the issue can add or remove links; read-only tokens are refused
- [ ] Issue view shows a "Pages" section listing the links with source icon and title
- [ ] `issue.updated` is not emitted for remote-link changes; a new `issue.remote_link.added|removed` topic is

## Tests

Unit tests for validation, integration tests including a raw-SQL RLS attempt, and an e2e scenario that adds a link via the API and sees it on the issue view.

issues.title: Documentation link in the project sidebar
issues.body:
## User story

As a team using Armature together with a documentation tool, I want a project to link to its documentation space, so that the docs are one click away from the board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Project settings accept an optional documentation URL and label
- [ ] When set, the project sidebar shows a "Docs" entry opening that URL
- [ ] Exposed on the project resource in the API so tools like Stator can set it (praetorianer777/Stator#83)

## Tests

Unit and integration tests for the setting, e2e scenario for the sidebar entry.

issues.title: Raise the subtle text colour to WCAG AA contrast
issues.body:
`--color-ink-subtle` (#8f877b light, #7d7569 dark) is below the WCAG AA contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against every surface token (`canvas`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `surface-sunken`, `surface-overlay`). axe's `color-contrast` rule flags every subtle label, placeholder and timestamp.

Stator, which shares Armature's design tokens, is adjusting the token by the smallest step that reaches 4.5:1 while keeping the hue (https://github.com/praetorianer777/Stator/issues/133). This issue proposes the same values for Armature, so both products stay identical. The exact values will be posted here once chosen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `--color-ink-subtle` values in `web/src/styles/index.css` (light and dark) and `docs/design/01-tokens.md`.
- [ ] A test that computes text/surface contrast for the token table in both modes.

issues.title: Emit issue.deleted, and issue.created for clones and imports
issues.body:
Deleting an issue emits no event, and cloning or importing one emits no `issue.created`. A webhook consumer such as Stator therefore keeps showing a deleted issue, and query results miss new issues, until its cache expires.

Please add a topic `issue.deleted` with payload `{issueId, key, actorId}`, available to webhook subscriptions, and emit `issue.created` for issues made by clone and by import.

Context: Stator clears its per-user issue cache on webhook events (praetorianer777/Stator#33).

issues.title: Report the calling token's scopes and projects in GET /auth/me
issues.body:
Called with a personal access token, `GET /auth/me` does not say whether the token has the read-only scope or is limited to certain projects. An integration therefore cannot warn at connect time that the token will fail to create issues or add remote links.

Please answer `token: {id, name, scopes, projects, expiresAt}` when the caller is a token, and `null` for a browser session.

Context: Stator's "Connect Armature" checks the token with `GET /auth/me` (praetorianer777/Stator#27).

issues.title: Sign a timestamp on webhook deliveries
issues.body:
Hardening, optional.

Deliveries carry no signed time, so receivers can only guard against replays by remembering event ids. Please add an `X-Armature-Timestamp` header and a second signature header, HMAC-SHA256 over `{timestamp}.{body}`. Receivers written for `X-Armature-Signature-256` keep working.

Context: Stator's webhook receiver currently remembers event ids for 24 hours instead (praetorianer777/Stator#33).

issues.title: Version the application with semantic versioning
issues.body:
## User story

As someone deploying Armature, I want every build to carry a semantic version and every release to be a tag, so that I know which version runs, can pin the chart to it and can read what changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `VERSION` file at the repository root is the single source of truth, starting at `0.1.0`
- [ ] `make release VERSION=x.y.z` refuses unless on a clean `main` with a valid semver greater than the current one, then writes `VERSION`, `web/package.json` and `Chart.yaml` (`version` and `appVersion`), moves `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` under the new version, regenerates the chart golden files, commits `Release x.y.z` and tags `vx.y.z` (no push)
- [ ] The backend image reports `x.y.z` on a tag, `x.y.z+<n>.g<sha>` past one, and `<VERSION>+dev` with no tag; `buildinfo` strips a leading `v`
- [ ] The Jenkinsfile tags images without the `v` so they match the chart's `appVersion`, passes the version build args, and no longer overwrites `latest` from branch builds
- [ ] `api/openapi.json` `info.version` stays the API contract number; the split is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`
- [ ] README gains a "Releasing" section; `CHANGELOG.md` exists

## Tests

A unit test refuses a `VERSION`, `web/package.json` and `Chart.yaml` that disagree. The release script is exercised against a scratch clone.

issues.title: Holiday calendars and working weeks
issues.body:
## User story

As an organization administrator with people in several countries, I want named holiday calendars and a working week per person, so that planning knows which days somebody can work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `holiday_calendar` (one default per organization), `holiday` (day, name, half day) and `member_schedule` (person, calendar or the default, minutes per weekday), with the usual tenant-isolation RLS and CHECKs mirroring the service's validation
- [ ] `member_schedule` admits only non-customer members of the organization, enforced by a trigger
- [ ] `GET/POST /holiday-calendars`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /holiday-calendars/{calendarID}`, `PUT .../days`, `POST .../import` (an `.ics` file, recurring events refused with a sentence) and `GET/PUT /users/{userID}/schedule`, in the route table, so they appear in `api/openapi.json` and as MCP tools
- [ ] Only organization administrators change calendars and other people's schedules; a person can read their own
- [ ] A settings page "Holidays" lists, edits and imports calendars; the users page sets a person's working week and calendar; the profile shows it read-only
- [ ] Every new organization gets an empty default calendar; the demo seed fills it with a few days

## Tests

Unit tests for the day arithmetic and the `.ics` parser, integration tests including raw-SQL RLS and guard attempts, and an e2e scenario that imports an `.ics` and sees the days.

issues.title: People record their absences
issues.body:
## User story

As a team member, I want to record when I am away, so that my colleagues and the plan stop counting on me for those days, without anyone learning why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `absence` (person, first day, last day, half day, created by) with no reason or note column; overlapping absences of one person are refused by the database
- [ ] `GET /absences`, `POST /absences`, `PATCH/DELETE /absences/{absenceID}`, in the route table
- [ ] A person records their own absences; an organization administrator, or a scrum master or project administrator of a team the person belongs to, may record them for that person; anyone else is refused
- [ ] Colleagues see only that the person is away; customers never see absences
- [ ] The profile page has an "Absences" section; the teams page lets a lead record one for a member
- [ ] `docs/privacy.md` and the privacy service cover absences: purpose, what is held, export, erasure, member removal and a retention window (`ARMATURE_RETAIN_ABSENCES`)

## Tests

Unit tests for validation, integration tests for every role case and a raw-SQL overlap and RLS attempt, vitest for the profile section, and an e2e scenario recording an absence.

Depends on #28.

issues.title: Holidays and absences on the calendar and in capacity
issues.body:
## User story

As a project member, I want holidays and my colleagues' absences on the calendar and taken out of capacity, so that the plan reflects who can actually work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One availability service combines working weeks, holiday calendars and absences into minutes available per person per day
- [ ] The project calendar shows holidays (shaded like weekends, with their name) and absences (the person and "away"), with a toggle to hide them
- [ ] The timeline shades the organization's default holidays
- [ ] Team load spreads estimates over working days only and scales each team's weekly capacity by its members' availability; the decision on team capacity is updated
- [ ] Sprint planning shows the team's available hours in the sprint window as a hint; capacity still warns and never refuses

## Tests

Unit tests for the availability service and the changed load spreading, integration tests for the calendar and plan responses, vitest for the month grid, and an e2e scenario where an absence appears on the project calendar.

Depends on #28 and #29.

issues.title: Resource planning per project: teams for scrum, teams or people for kanban
issues.body:
## User story

As a project lead, I want a resource planning view that sets the work scheduled against the hours available per week, by team for a scrum project and by team or by person for a kanban project, so that I see who is overloaded before it happens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Projects gain a planning method (`scrum` or `kanban`, backfilled from their boards, new projects from their template) and a resource grouping (`team` or `person`); the database refuses grouping by person on a scrum project
- [ ] Project settings choose the method and, for kanban, the grouping
- [ ] A new project feature "Resources" adds a sidebar page
- [ ] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/resources?from&to`, in the route table, returns per row (team or person) and per week the capacity in hours, the load in hours, the contributing issues and the days away
- [ ] Load is an issue's remaining time (or its estimate) spread over the row's working days between start and due; unscheduled and unestimated work is listed, not guessed
- [ ] Rows over capacity carry an `over-allocated` warning; nothing is refused
- [ ] The page draws a row per team or person and a column per week, holidays and absences hatched, and lists the issues of a week on click

## Tests

Unit tests for grouping and spreading, integration tests including the raw-SQL scrum guard and refusals, vitest for the page, and e2e scenarios for a kanban project switching to people and a scrum project offering only teams.

Depends on #30.

issues.title: A team manager can change any member's absences by adding them to a team
issues.body:
## User story

As a member of an organization, I want only my own team's managers to be able to change my absences, so that someone who simply adds me to a team cannot rewrite the days I am away.

## What happens today

`mayRecord` in `backend/internal/availability/absence_service.go` lets someone record, change or delete a person's absences in three cases:
- they are that person;
- they hold `org.administer`;
- they hold `team.manage` in a project where that person is on a team.

A team manager also decides who is on their teams: `POST /teams/{teamID}/members` accepts any non-customer member of the organization. So a scrum master of any project can take over anybody's absences in two requests:

1. `POST /api/v1/teams/{theirTeam}/members {"userId": "<anyone, an org admin included>"}`
2. `POST /api/v1/absences {"userId": ...}`, or `PATCH` / `DELETE /api/v1/absences/{id}` with an id from `GET /absences`.

The impact is limited to planning data. No reason is stored, nothing becomes readable that was not already, and both steps land in the audit log. It is still a way around the rule the feature was built on (#29): only the person, an administrator or *their* team's manager.

Found in the security review of #32 and #37 (confidence 4/10, below the bar for a vulnerability).

## Acceptance criteria

A check on team membership alone cannot close this. The manager controls the team, so "was on the team before this request" only means waiting a minute, and project read access comes from org-wide roles too. The fix limits what a manager may do and makes it visible:

- [ ] A team manager may record an absence for a member of their team, but may change or delete only absences they recorded themselves (`created_by`). The person's own entries, and an administrator's, are out of a manager's reach.
- [ ] When someone other than the person records, changes or removes their absence, the person is told through the inbox (and mail, if they asked for it), without the dates in the mail.
- [ ] An administrator and the person themselves are unaffected.
- [ ] A refusal is a 403 with a sentence that names who to ask instead, for example "Only Ada or an administrator can change this absence."
- [ ] The rule is written in `docs/decisions.md` next to "An absence says when, never why, and nobody approves it", and `docs/privacy.md` says accurately who may change someone's absences.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - a scrum master cannot change or delete an absence the person or an administrator recorded;
  - a scrum master can still change one they recorded;
  - the person gets an inbox entry each time someone else touches their absences;
  - the person and an administrator keep full control.
- **Proven in SQL as well:** if the rule moves into the database, prove it there too, as CLAUDE.md asks.
- **Browser:** the person sees the notice in their inbox after a scrum master records an absence for them.

issues.title: One issue dated far in the future makes every plan load build availability for centuries
issues.body:
## What happens today

`plan.Window()` (`backend/internal/plan/plan.go:236-252`) stretches to the earliest start and the latest due date of the scheduled work, with no cap. Issue dates have no bound beyond `start_date <= due_date` (`migrations/00006_planning.sql:12`).

`plan/service.go:179` and `:202` then call `availability.ForPeople(ctx, ids, first, last)` over that window. `Schedule.Days` (`availability/people.go:68-75`) makes one `PersonDay` per calendar day per person, and `plan/workdays.go:31-38` indexes all of them into maps.

The resource view clamps the same read to `reachDays = 366` (`plan/resources_service.go:51-52`). The plan does not.

**Scenario:** someone types a due date of 2206 instead of 2026, or 9999-12-31. Every `GET /projects/{key}/plan` now builds millions of `PersonDay`s per team member. That costs hundreds of MB and seconds of CPU on every page view, for everyone who opens the plan.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The plan reads availability over a bounded span around the visible window, as the resource view does. Work outside it still spreads, over calendar days.
- [ ] Issue dates outside a sane range (for example 1970 to 2200) are refused with a sentence, in the service and by a CHECK.
- [ ] The timeline still opens on the right window for ordinary projects.

## Tests

- **Unit:** `Window` and the availability span with a far-future due date.
- **Integration:**
  - a plan with one issue due in 9999 answers quickly and carries no day beyond the bound;
  - a raw `UPDATE issue SET due_date = '9999-12-31'` is refused by the CHECK.

issues.title: The resources page counts a parent's hours and its children's hours, so the work is booked twice
issues.body:
## What happens today

`plan/resources.go:166-184` spreads every open issue that has hours into its row. The `parents` map (`:160-165`) is only used to keep parents out of the Unestimated list. Time fields are stored per issue and are not rolled up.

The team load and the sprints count work once, at whichever level carries it (`topmostByTeam` in `load.go:397`, `topmostBySprint` in `capacity.go:123`, and the decision "Work in a sprint is counted once, at whichever level carries it"). The resource view does not.

**Scenario:**
1. A story is estimated at 16 h and has two subtasks of 8 h each.
2. All three are scheduled in the same week on team A.

The cell shows 32 h, and the warning says 32 h are allocated against 40 h. With a second story like it the team reads as over-allocated when it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An issue whose ancestor already carries hours on the same row is not counted again, the same rule as the team load.
- [ ] When the parent has no hours, the children's hours are counted as today.
- [ ] The cell's issue list says which issues were counted.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the story and subtasks above read 16 h, and a parent without hours plus two 8 h children reads 16 h.
- **Integration:** the resources response for that hierarchy.

issues.title: Someone who left the organization still shows on the resources page with a full week free
issues.body:
## What happens today

Removing a member deletes their `team_member`, `member_schedule` and `absence` rows, but leaves them as the assignee of their issues (`privacy/service.go:477-489`).

- Person rows are built from every open issue's assignee (`plan/resources.go:222-226`).
- `ProjectPeople` joins only `app_user`, not `org_member` (`availability/people_service.go:375-382`).
- `ForPeople` finds no schedule for them, so `combine` gives them `StandardWeek()` (`people.go:105-108`).

**Scenario:** in a kanban project grouped by person, Alice leaves while three open issues dated next month are still assigned to her. The grid shows an "Alice" row with 40 of 40 h, and her work counts as placed instead of being flagged as nobody's.

The same assignees reach the project calendar's absence list and the team load's people.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An assignee who is no longer a non-customer member of the organization gets no row with capacity. Their work goes to Unassigned, or to a row that says they have left, with 0 h available.
- [ ] The over-allocated warnings and the unscheduled lists still count that work.

## Tests

- **Unit:** an assignee with no membership.
- **Integration:** remove a member who still holds dated work, then read the resources by person.

issues.title: Say what share of a person's week belongs to a project, so people on two projects are not counted twice
issues.body:
## User story

As a kanban lead, I want to say that Bob gives half his week to this project, so that the resources page measures his work here against 20 h and not the 40 h his week holds.

## What happens today

Person and team rows take their capacity from the whole working week (`hoursOfWeek` with `peopleTime`, `plan/resources.go:208, 266-270`; `workdays.go:98-125`). The availability tables hold a week and absences (migrations `00909`, `00910`). Nothing stores how a person's week is split between projects.

So Bob, who works half on A and half on B, shows 40 h available in both. Neither project warns, even when he carries 30 h in each.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project administrator can set a share (a percentage, 100 by default) per person for the project, and per team member for team rows.
- [ ] Capacity and nominal hours on the resources page are scaled by the share. The tooltip says so, for example "20 of 20 h (50% of the week)".
- [ ] The total of a person's shares across projects is shown where it is set. Going over 100% warns and never refuses, like capacity elsewhere.
- [ ] The share is in `docs/decisions.md` next to "Resource planning is in hours; team capacity stays in points".

## Tests

- **Unit:** the scaled capacity, and a share of 0.
- **Integration:**
  - setting and reading the share;
  - the refusal for someone without project administration;
  - the resources response with a share, contract-validated.
- **Vitest:** the share editor and the tooltip.
- **Browser:** setting 50% halves a person's week on the page.

issues.title: An .ics event with DURATION is imported as one day, and one whose DTEND equals DTSTART refuses the whole file
issues.body:
## What happens today

`availability/ics.go:64-78` reads DTSTART, DTEND, SUMMARY, RRULE/RDATE and STATUS. DURATION is never read. In `days()` (`ics.go:112-123`), an event with no DTEND lasts one day, and `!end.After(start)` refuses DTEND == DTSTART with "ends before it starts".

RFC 5545 allows DURATION in place of DTEND, and some exporters write a same-day DTEND for a one-day event.

**Scenario:**
- A feed with `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261224` and `DURATION:P3D` imports only 24 December. The 25th and 26th are silently missing.
- A file with `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20261224` on that same event is refused as a whole.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A day-only DURATION (`PnD`, `PnW`) sets the end. A DURATION with a time part is refused with a sentence that says to export whole days.
- [ ] DTEND equal to DTSTART reads as that one day.
- [ ] DTEND before DTSTART is still refused, with the event's name.

## Tests

- **Unit:** `P3D`, `P1W`, `PT8H` (refused), DTEND == DTSTART, and DTEND before DTSTART.

issues.title: Importing an .ics file again turns the calendar's half-day holidays into whole days off
issues.body:
## What happens today

`ImportICS` always builds `Holiday{..., HalfDay: false}` (`availability/ics.go:91`). `Import` writes the days through `putDays`, which upserts with `ON CONFLICT (calendar_id, day) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, half_day = EXCLUDED.half_day` (`availability/service.go:293-297`).

The documented contract says a day the calendar already has takes only the file's name: `service.go:251-252`, the operation summary in `openapi_operations.go:178`, and the hook comment in `web/src/api/availability.ts:93`.

**Scenario:**
1. An admin marks 24 and 31 December as half days.
2. They import the regional .ics again, to add next year.

Both days become whole days off, and every team's capacity for those weeks drops without anyone noticing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An import leaves `half_day` alone on a day the calendar already holds, and updates only the name.
- [ ] Replacing the days from the editor still writes `half_day` as given.

## Tests

- **Integration:** mark a half day, import a file holding that day, and read it back as a half day with the file's name.

issues.title: An absence more than a year ahead disappears from the editor as soon as it is saved
issues.body:
## What happens today

The server accepts any start date (`CheckAbsence`, `availability/absence.go:67-85`). The editors list absences through `useAbsences({ userId })` with no `from` or `to` (`web/src/features/availability/Absences.tsx:110`, `web/src/routes/profile.tsx:196`). The server then lists from 31 days ago to 365 days ahead (`AbsenceWindow`, `absence.go:89-103`), and the list has no way to page through dates.

**Scenario:** on 2026-10-08 someone records parental leave from 2027-11-01.
1. The toast says "Absence recorded".
2. The list still says they are not away in the last month or the year ahead.
3. They cannot see, change or remove that absence in the UI until next month.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The editor lists every absence of the person from a month ago onwards, with no upper bound, or it offers a way to page forward.
- [ ] An absence saved outside what the list shows is never hidden silently: the list widens, or the toast says where to find it.
- [ ] The list stays bounded server side (for example, no more than a set number of rows) and says when it is cut.

## Tests

- **Integration:** list one person's absences with only `from` given, and see one 14 months ahead.
- **Vitest:** the editor shows a far-future absence straight after saving it.

issues.title: The project calendar leaves holidays and absences off the neighbouring months' days, and cuts an absence at the month's end
issues.body:
## What happens today

`calendar.Month` reads days off only from the 1st to the last of the month (`backend/internal/calendar/calendar.go:168`). `daysOff` clips each absence to that span: `From: max(a.StartsOn, from), To: min(a.EndsOn, to)` (`:203-208`).

The grid draws 42 cells, including days of the months before and after (`web/src/features/calendar/grid.ts:42-53`), and places items on them (`MonthGrid.tsx:106-131`). Issue bars are not clipped, so the two kinds disagree on the same cells.

**Scenario:** Bob is away from 28 September to 9 October, and 3 October is a holiday.
- In the September view his bar ends with a rounded cap on 30 September, as if he were back on 1 October.
- The 1 to 4 October cells show issues, but no absence and no holiday shading.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Holidays and absences are read over the six weeks the grid shows.
- [ ] An absence that runs past the shown range is drawn as continuing, the way an issue bar is.
- [ ] `MaxItems` and the truncation notice still apply.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the September month carries the October holiday and the whole absence.
- **Vitest:** an absence that continues past the grid is drawn open-ended.

issues.title: Carry a holiday calendar's fixed-date holidays into the next year
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want New Year, 1 May and Christmas to carry into next year, so that I do not have to type or import every calendar again each January, and the plan does not quietly count those days as working days.

## What happens today

A holiday is one dated row (`migrations/00909_holiday_calendars.sql:28-40`). There is no recurrence and no copy endpoint (`routes_organization.go:81-92`), and `CalendarDays.tsx` offers only "Add a day" and "Import .ics". The decisions cover refusing RRULE in imports, not repeating fixed dates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A "Copy to next year" action on a calendar proposes this year's days moved to the same dates next year, as an unsaved draft the administrator reviews. Movable feasts such as Easter are then corrected by hand or by import.
- [ ] Or a holiday can be marked "every year", stored as month and day and expanded when read. Pick one and write the choice in `docs/decisions.md` next to "Holidays are named calendars a person is given".
- [ ] Copying never overwrites a day the next year already holds.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the copy, including 29 February.
- **Integration:** the endpoint (success, refusal for a non-administrator), contract-validated.
- **Browser:** copy, review, save, and see next year's days on the calendar.

issues.title: The resources page opens on the wrong week around midnight for people outside UTC
issues.body:
## What happens today

`web/src/routes/resources.tsx:28` and `:57` call `mondayOf(new Date())`. `mondayOf` (`web/src/features/resources/cells.ts:211-215`) goes through `day()`, which takes the UTC fields (`web/src/features/plan/scale.ts:60-63`).

`today()` in `web/src/lib/week.ts:46-49` deliberately uses the local date, "the day they mean by today". The decision "Dates are the reader's, not the browser's" asks for the same here.

**Scenario:**
- In Berlin at 00:30 on Monday (Sunday 22:30 UTC), the page opens on last week, and so does "Today".
- In New York on Sunday evening (Monday UTC), it jumps to next week.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The page's starting week and "Today" are the Monday of the reader's local date.
- [ ] The dates sent to the API are unchanged in form (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

## Tests

- **Vitest:** `mondayOf` (or the route's start) with a fake clock at Monday 00:30 in UTC+2, and at Sunday 20:00 in UTC-4.

issues.title: Importing an .ics file throws away the holiday table's unsaved edits without asking
issues.body:
## What happens today

In `web/src/features/availability/CalendarDays.tsx:28-40`, the import's `onSuccess` calls `setDraft(null)`. The Import button stays enabled while a draft exists (`:53-55`).

**Scenario:**
1. An admin adds three days by hand and does not press "Save days".
2. They import a file.

The three days are gone, and the toast only says "Added N days".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While the table has unsaved edits, importing either asks first ("Import and discard 3 unsaved days?"), or merges the imported days into the draft. Pick one.
- [ ] Nothing typed is lost without the person saying so.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** with a draft open, importing asks (or merges) and keeps the typed days until confirmed.

issues.title: Reach every unscheduled and unestimated issue from the resources page, not only the first 25
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead tidying up a plan, I want to open the whole list of work the resources page could not place, so that I can date and estimate it, not only the first 25.

## What happens today

`web/src/features/resources/UnplacedWork.tsx:24-44` cuts each list to `RESOURCE_LIST_LIMIT` (25, `config.ts:345`) and prints "and N more" as plain text. The backend already returns the full lists (`plan/resources.go:172-176`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "and N more" expands the list in place, or links to the issue search with the matching query (open issues in the project with no start or due date, or no estimate).
- [ ] If it links, the query is the same one the page uses, so the counts agree.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the expand (or the link and its query) with 30 issues.

issues.title: Configure swimlanes always edits the project's first board, and a board cannot be renamed or removed
issues.body:
## What happens today

- **Wrong board:** `web/src/routes/board.tsx:93` passes the shown board's id to `BoardView`, but `:100` renders `<SwimlaneEditor projectKey={projectKey} />` with no board. The editor reads `useBoard(projectKey)` (`SwimlaneEditor.tsx:31`).
- **Server side:** every swimlane route is `/projects/{projectKey}/board/swimlanes...`. `board/configure.go:45,109,159,191` resolve the board with `boardIDFor`, which is `ORDER BY b.created_at LIMIT 1` (`:260-266`).
- **Grouping:** the grouping chips call `SetGrouping`, which runs `UPDATE board SET group_by ... WHERE project_id = ...` over every board in the project (`board/service.go:539-547`). `PATCH /boards/{id}` can already set it per board.
- **No board management:** `useUpdateBoard` and `useDeleteBoard` (`web/src/api/boards.ts:144-159`) have no caller, so a board made by mistake cannot be renamed, retyped or removed.

**Scenario:**
1. Make a team board, pick it, and press Configure swimlanes.
2. The panel lists and edits the first board's lanes and WIP limits.
3. Picking "Assignee" regroups every board in the project.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Swimlanes and WIP limits are read and written per board, through board-addressed routes (`/boards/{boardID}/swimlanes...`). The old project-addressed routes go, or keep meaning the first board and say so.
- [ ] The editor edits the board on screen.
- [ ] Grouping is set per board.
- [ ] The board picker offers Rename, Change type and Delete, with Delete confirming with the board's name.
- [ ] `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Integration:** lanes of a second board, the refusal for a reader, and a raw SQL check that lanes stay with their board.
- **Vitest:** the editor gets the shown board's id.
- **Browser:** configure a team board's lanes and see the first board unchanged.

issues.title: The Sprints page reads only the project's 200 newest issues, so older committed work and backlog go missing
issues.body:
## What happens today

`web/src/features/sprints/SprintPlanning.tsx:32` calls `useIssues({ project, limit: MAX_PAGE_SIZE })` (200, `config.ts:7`; the list is ordered by `created_at DESC`, `issue/list.go:98`). The backlog (`:44`) and every sprint's contents (`:76`) are filtered out of that one page, and nothing leaves out resolved issues.

The ranked, uncapped `/boards/{id}/backlog` (`team_handlers.go:212`, `useBacklog` in `api/boards.ts:118-124`) has no caller. The parent picker has the same cap (`features/issues/hierarchy.tsx:214`), so parents past it are never offered.

**Scenario:** in a project with 250 issues, KEY-10 is committed to Sprint 3.
1. Its sprint card does not list it, while the card's totals count its points.
2. The card looks empty, so "Delete" is offered (shown when `issues.length === 0`), and deleting the sprint sends hidden work back to the backlog.
3. "Backlog (n)" also counts resolved issues that were never in a sprint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The backlog is read from the server, ranked and without the cap, and leaves out the done category.
- [ ] Each sprint's contents are read for that sprint.
- [ ] A sprint is offered for deletion only when the server says it is empty.
- [ ] The parent picker searches instead of offering a capped list.

## Tests

- **Integration:** a sprint-scoped read with more than 200 project issues.
- **Vitest:** the planning page draws a sprint's issues from the sprint read.
- **Browser:** a project seeded past 200 issues shows an old committed issue in its sprint.

issues.title: Let finished work leave a kanban board, so the done lane and its WIP count stop growing forever
issues.body:
## User story

As a kanban team, I want work finished a while ago to leave the board, so that the Done column stays readable and the board loads quickly a year in.

## What happens today

With no sprint scope, `loadCards` (`backend/internal/board/service.go:354-370`) reads `WHERE i.project_id = $1 AND t.hierarchy_level >= $2`, with no status, `resolved_at` or row limit. `BoardView.tsx:250` counts `swimlane.cards.length` against the WIP limit.

After a year the Done column holds thousands of cards, the payload grows without bound, and a WIP limit on a lane holding a done status is always exceeded. The README says "kanban shows everything", and the plan already has the idea "Closed work leaves the plan after a number of days the reader chooses".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A kanban board leaves out done-category issues resolved more than N days ago, N set per board (for example 14 by default, 0 meaning never).
- [ ] The board says how many finished issues it is leaving out, with a link to search for them.
- [ ] WIP limits count only what the board shows.
- [ ] The rule is written next to "A board is scoped by team, and its type is behaviour".

## Tests

- **Integration:** an issue resolved 30 days ago is not on a board set to 14 days; the setting is refused for a reader.
- **Browser:** the hidden count on a seeded board.

issues.title: Deleting a team hands its sprints, a running one included, to the project, or fails with a 500
issues.body:
## What happens today

`team.Service.Delete` (`backend/internal/team/service.go:230-248`) refuses only while the team has issues or boards, and never counts sprints.
- `sprint.team_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`migrations/00009_teams.sql:79`).
- One running sprint per stream is enforced by a unique index on `(project_id, team_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE state='active'` (`:86`).
- `request_type.team_id` (00025) is also SET NULL.

**Scenario:**
- If the project's own stream already has a running sprint, deleting a team that still has one raises a unique violation. It is not mapped, so the person gets a 500.
- Otherwise the team's running sprint silently becomes the project's. Its closed sprints join the project-level velocity and sprint history.
- Request types routed to the team quietly stop routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deleting a team that still has sprints is refused with a sentence naming them ("Team Alpha still has 4 sprints, one of them running. Complete or move them first."), the same as for issues and boards. Or the sprints are deleted or archived with the team, and that is decided and written down.
- [ ] Request types routed to the team are named in the refusal, or are reset with the person told so.
- [ ] The database refuses the same thing: a raw `DELETE FROM team` with sprints fails.

## Tests

- **Integration:** both scenarios above, the refusal text, and the raw SQL delete.

issues.title: An issue whose team differs from its sprint's team vanishes from the Sprints page but still counts in the sprint
issues.body:
## What happens today

Nothing compares an issue's team with its sprint's team:
- `SetTeam` and `SetSprint` (`issue/sprint.go`) do not.
- The triggers in 00008/00009 do not.
- Sprint completion's carry-over (`sprint/lifecycle.go` `resolveDestination`) accepts another team's sprint.

`SprintPlanning.tsx:42` filters issues by the selected stream's team first, and `:76` then picks each sprint's issues out of that list.

**Scenario:** KEY-5 is in Team A's running sprint, and someone hands KEY-5 to Team B.
- It is not in A's sprint card, because it is the wrong team.
- It is not in B's backlog, because it has a sprint.
- It is not in any of B's sprints.
- A's committed points still include it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Changing an issue's team takes it out of a sprint that belongs to another stream, and the history says so. Or the change is refused with a sentence. Pick one and write it next to "One running sprint per stream, and planning is the team's work".
- [ ] `SetSprint` and carry-over into another team's sprint are refused, in the service and by a trigger.

## Tests

- **Integration:** both paths, plus a raw `UPDATE issue SET sprint_id` into another team's sprint, refused.

issues.title: A dashboard saved as a template keeps its pinned version, so its release widgets break in other projects
issues.body:
## What happens today

`backend/internal/report/templates.go:230` clears `TeamID`, `SprintID` and `MilestoneID` before saving a widget into a template ("mean nothing in the next project"), but not `VersionID`.

- The Releases widget filters `v.project_id = $1 AND (... OR v.id = $3)` and comes back empty.
- Release burndown (`report/flow.go:484`) answers "that version is not one of this project's".

**Scenario:**
1. Pin a Releases widget to v1.2 in project A.
2. Save the dashboard as a template.
3. Create a dashboard from it in project B.

The Releases widget is empty and Release burndown shows an error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `VersionID` is cleared along with the others, and any other project-bound widget parameter is too.
- [ ] Templates already saved with a version id read as if it were unset in other projects.

## Tests

- **Unit:** `ParamsFrom` after templating has no version.
- **Integration:** a template saved from A, used in B, shows all unreleased versions.

issues.title: On a shared dashboard, the Sprint history widget's Curve button fails for visitors
issues.body:
## What happens today

`web/src/features/dashboard/WidgetBody.tsx:304-311` (`PastBurndown`) calls `useReport(projectKey, "burndown", { sprintId })` without a `widgetId`. `api/reports.tsx:406` uses the shared route only when a `widgetId` is given, so the request goes to the signed-in `/projects/{key}/reports/burndown` and gets a 401. Unlike MilestonesBody and FlowBodies, the button is not hidden when `readOnly`.

**Scenario:** share a dashboard with Sprint history, open the link signed out, and press Curve. An error shows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a shared dashboard the past sprint's curve loads through the share, limited to the sprints that widget lists. Or the button is hidden when read-only.
- [ ] The share still reaches nothing beyond its widgets.

## Tests

- **Integration (if served):** the share route answers a listed sprint, and refuses one not listed.
- **Vitest:** read-only rendering.

issues.title: Behind a load balancer, an older write's position can overwrite a newer one and break read-your-writes
issues.body:
## What happens today

`RedisTracker.Note` (`backend/internal/freshness/freshness.go:45-52`) is an unconditional `SET`. `MemoryTracker.Note` (`:90-94`) guards `cur.lsn >= lsn`, with the comment "requests can complete out of order". The Redis tracker, the one used with more than one API process, has no such guard.

**Scenario:**
1. Two writes from one session commit at LSN 100 and LSN 90, and the second `Note` lands last.
2. Redis now holds 90.
3. The next read may be sent to a replica at 95, which misses the person's own write at 100.

This undoes "Read replicas with read-your-writes".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The stored position only ever rises: a Lua script that sets only when greater, keeping the TTL.
- [ ] Failure stays best effort, as today.

## Tests

- **Integration (against the stack's Valkey):** `Note(100)` then `Note(90)` leaves 100; `Note(110)` raises it.

issues.title: Release burndown counts issues as remaining on days before they were filed
issues.body:
## What happens today

`backend/internal/report/flow.go:495-510` takes `fixing` as every current fix issue of the version. Each day counts `f.resolved_at IS NULL OR f.resolved_at >= d.day + 1 day`, with no `created_at` condition. The series also runs to today for a version released long ago.

**Scenario:** a version starts on 1 March with 5 issues, and 10 more are filed on 20 March. The chart shows 15 remaining from 1 March, so the scope growth is hidden and the line looks flat.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An issue counts on a day only if it existed then: `created_at < day + 1`. The scope line rises when work is added.
- [ ] A released version's series stops at its release day.
- [ ] Adding an issue to a version later is still counted from its filing. Counting from when it joined the version needs the version changelog; note it if not done.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the scenario above, and a released version's series ending on its day.

issues.title: The burndown draws nothing on a sprint's first day and misplaces points when a sprint starts early or ends late
issues.body:
## What happens today

- **First day:** `Start` writes one snapshot and the report swaps today for the live point, so the series has one point. `pathOf` (`web/src/features/dashboard/charts.tsx:191`) turns one point into just `M x y`, which draws nothing, and only the dashed ideal line shows.
- **Started early:** `burndown.ts:6-8,29` counts x from `sprint.startsOn`. A sprint started before its date gets a negative x, drawn outside the view box (`overflow-visible`).
- **Ended late:** `LineChart` (`:141`) stretches to the largest x, but `axisLabels` (`:56`) always puts `endsOn` at the right edge. A sprint completed two days late is labelled two days early.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A one-point series draws a marker.
- [ ] The x span runs from the earlier of `startsOn` and the first point to the later of `endsOn` and the last point, and the labels come from that same span.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** a one-point curve, a sprint started two days early, and a sprint ended two days late.

issues.title: The hourly snapshot can overwrite a just-completed sprint's last burndown point
issues.body:
## What happens today

`sprint/snapshots.go` `Once` lists the active sprints, then calls `Snapshot` for each. `Snapshot` (`snapshot.go:42-60`) never checks the state again, and `writeSnapshot` upserts on `(sprint_id, day)`. `Complete` (`lifecycle.go`) writes the day's last point before it moves the unfinished work out.

**Scenario:**
1. The worker lists sprint S as active.
2. S is completed, and its unfinished issues go back to the backlog.
3. The worker counts S, which now holds only the done work, and replaces today's row.

The closed sprint's burndown ends at "0 remaining", with scope equal to completed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A snapshot is written only for a sprint that is active inside the writing transaction (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the sprint).
- [ ] A completed sprint's stored report and last point are never changed by the worker.

## Tests

- **Integration:** call `Snapshot` on a sprint completed in between, and see the completion point unchanged.

issues.title: Quick filters on a board: mine, by assignee, label, type or epic, and a text search
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working from a busy board, I want to narrow it to my cards or to one epic's, so that I can find my work without making a new board.

## What happens today

`web/src/features/board/BoardView.tsx` and `routes/board.tsx` have no filter controls. The only scope a board's cards have is team or sprint (`board/service.go` `cardScope`), which is stored with the board. Nothing narrows it for the moment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chips above the board: Only mine, Assignee, Label, Type, Epic, and a text box matching key and summary.
- [ ] They filter the cards already loaded, and say how many are hidden.
- [ ] The choice is kept in the URL, so a filtered board can be linked.
- [ ] WIP counts stay on the whole lane, and say so when filtered.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** each chip, the combination, and the URL round trip.
- **Browser:** Only mine on the seeded board.

issues.title: A customer's reply to a resolved request does not reopen it, though the resolution mail says it will
issues.body:
## What happens today

The resolution mail tells the customer to "reply on the request and it comes back to us" (`desk/mail.go:103`). `Reply` (`desk/service.go:1047-1069`) moves the request only when its status is `WaitingOnCustomer`. The service template has a Reopen transition from Resolved (`template/template.go:137`) that nothing takes.

Inbound mail from the reporter goes through the same `Reply` (`desk/inbound.go:212`). A follower's mail goes through `AddComment` and never moves the request at all (`:209`).

**Scenario:** the request is resolved, and the customer answers "still broken" in the portal or by mail.
- The comment is added, but the request stays Resolved.
- It is not in the Open, Unassigned or Mine queues, and no clock restarts.

The reply is in effect lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reply from the reporter or a follower to a request in the done category takes the workflow's way back out of done (Reopen in the template), as the customer.
- [ ] The resolution clock restarts as it does for any reopen.
- [ ] If the workflow offers no way out, the request stays put and the agents are told in the inbox.
- [ ] A rated request reopened this way keeps its rating as history.

## Tests

- **Integration:** a portal reply reopens, a mailed reply reopens, a follower's mailed reply reopens, and a workflow without a way out leaves an inbox note.
- **Browser:** reply on a resolved request in the portal and see it back in the agents' Open queue.

issues.title: Out-of-office replies are posted as the customer's answer and take a request out of Waiting for customer
issues.body:
## What happens today

`mailin/parse.go:79-81` sets `AutoSubmitted` from `Auto-Submitted` and `Precedence`. `desk/inbound.go` reads it only to hold back the bounce (`:325`). It is never checked before the mail is turned into a comment (`:195-213`, ending in `n.desk.Reply`).

**Scenario:**
1. An agent replies and moves the request to Waiting for customer.
2. The customer's mail server answers with an out-of-office (`Auto-Submitted: auto-replied`).
3. It is posted as a public comment, the request goes back to In progress, and the paused clocks start again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A matched mail that is auto-submitted (`Auto-Submitted` other than `no`, `X-Autoreply`, `X-Autorespond`, `Precedence: auto_reply`/`bulk`/`junk`/`list`) is recorded with its own outcome and never commented.
- [ ] The mail is still deleted from the box, and the inbound log says why it was skipped.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the header combinations.
- **Integration:** an auto-reply to a waiting request leaves the status, the comments and the clocks unchanged.

issues.title: Resolving a request without a public reply leaves its first-response clock running into a breach
issues.body:
## What happens today

In the clock update (`desk/service.go:654-684`), only `t.Metric == Resolution && toDone` completes a clock. A first-response timer has no case for done. `desk/watch.go` does not look at the status, and `report/reports.go:537-545` counts the breach.

**Scenario:** an agent resolves a duplicate with no public comment, or the customer resolves it themselves. Hours later the worker emits `sla.breached` ("missed its first response goal") to the agents, and the SLA report counts a breach on a closed request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Moving to the done category completes every open clock: first response as well as resolution. A breach that had already happened is kept.
- [ ] Reopening restarts resolution as today. First response stays answered once it has been.
- [ ] The rule is written next to "The clocks move inside the issue's transaction".

## Tests

- **Integration:** resolve with no reply, advance the clock past the goal, and see no breach and no event. Resolve after a breach, and see the breach kept.

issues.title: Transition on merge fires again on every later delivery about an already merged pull request
issues.body:
## What happens today

In `git/service.go:494-508` the upsert returns `wasState` from a subquery with `q.id <> pull_request.id`. That can never match under `UNIQUE (repository_id, number)`, so `wasState` is always empty, and it is never read anyway. Line 546 queues the merge transition whenever `pr.State == PullMerged`.

**Scenario:**
1. A PR is merged and its issue moves to Done.
2. The issue is reopened.
3. Someone labels or edits the merged PR, or the host redelivers the event (the payload still says merged).
4. The issue is moved to Done again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The merge transition and the branch's merged mark act only when a pull request changes to merged, read from the row as it was before the upsert (a CTE selecting it first, or `xmax = 0` together with the old state).
- [ ] A redelivered merge event does nothing the second time.

## Tests

- **Integration:** deliver a merge, reopen the issue, deliver an edit of the merged PR, and see the issue stay open; then redeliver the same merge payload.

issues.title: Squash and merge commits run a branch's smart commands a second time
issues.body:
## What happens today

Smart commands run once for each newly recorded commit SHA (`git/service.go:576-592`). A GitHub squash commit copies every commit message of the branch into one new SHA, and a merge commit often carries the PR title.

The decision "Smart commits act once" says merging a branch is not a second `#close`. That holds only for a fast-forward.

**Scenario:**
1. A push of "ABC-1 #comment fixed typo" posts a comment.
2. Squash-merging the PR pushes a new commit whose body holds "* ABC-1 #comment fixed typo".
3. The comment is posted again. A `#close` in it is tried again and refused, which clutters the receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A command already carried out from this repository on the same issue, with the same text, is not carried out again. This needs a record of commands carried out, keyed by repository, issue and command text.
- [ ] A genuinely new command in a squash commit's message still runs.
- [ ] The decision is updated to say how squash and merge commits are treated.

## Tests

- **Unit:** command identity.
- **Integration:** a push with a comment command, then a squash commit carrying the same line, posts one comment.

issues.title: The agent queues read only the 200 newest requests, so the oldest and most overdue ones disappear
issues.body:
## What happens today

`desk/service.go:757-758` lists `issues.List(..., Limit: 200, OrderBy: "created", Desc: true)` (`queueSize`). The breached filter (around `:808`) and `sortByUrgency` then run on that page only.

**Scenario:** a desk has 250 open requests. The 50 oldest, which are the ones most likely to have breached, are in neither Open nor Breached.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Queues are ordered and limited in SQL by urgency (breached first, then the least time left), not by creation.
- [ ] A queue longer than a page can be paged, and says how many it holds.
- [ ] Breached shows every breached open request.

## Tests

- **Integration:** 250 requests with the oldest breached; Breached lists them, and the Open queue's first page starts with them.

issues.title: A pull request's CI badge shows only the most recently started check, so a failing PR can read green
issues.body:
## What happens today

`git/service.go:867` orders runs by `started_at DESC`, and `:885-893` take the first run whose SHA is the head ("the one answer to 'is it green'"). GitHub sends a separate check run per job, plus a workflow run.

**Scenario:** on the head SHA, "test" fails at 10:00 and "lint" passes, started at 10:01. The PR shows success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The badge for a head SHA combines the latest run per check name: any failure is failure, else any pending is pending, else success.
- [ ] The issue's development panel can list the checks behind the badge.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the combination rule.
- **Integration:** two runs on one SHA, one failed and one passed later, read as failed.

issues.title: A branch the host deletes after merging disappears from its issue's development panel
issues.body:
## What happens today

`git/service.go:393` runs `DELETE FROM git_branch WHERE repository_id = $1 AND name = $2` on any branch delete. The merged mark set at `:539-545` goes with the row. GitLab's "delete source branch" and GitHub's "automatically delete head branches" make this the normal flow. The model comment promises that "merging the pull request ... marks it merged, so the issue shows how far its branch has come".

**Scenario:** a branch made from ABC-1 is merged through a PR, and the host deletes it straight away. The panel no longer shows the branch or that it was merged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A merged branch that is deleted on the host is kept, marked deleted, and shown as "merged, deleted".
- [ ] An unmerged branch that is deleted is still removed, or shown as deleted. Decide which.
- [ ] A branch of the same name pushed again later is a new branch.

## Tests

- **Integration:** merge then delete keeps the branch with both marks; delete without merge removes it.

issues.title: Customers can raise a new request by mailing the desk
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer, I want to mail support@ about a new problem and have it become a request, so that I do not have to find the portal first.

## What happens today

`desk/inbound.go:170-172`: a mail that names no request is recorded as Unmatched and answered with "use the portal". Nothing raises a request from mail. The decision "Replies come in by POP3" covers replies only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A desk can name a default request type for mail. An unmatched mail that passes the sender's own server checks and the desk's trusted domains raises a request of that type, with the sender as reporter (a customer without a password, as followers already are). Its subject becomes the summary, its text the description, and its attachments the request's files.
- [ ] A desk without a mail request type keeps today's refusal.
- [ ] Auto-submitted mail never raises a request.
- [ ] The decision is extended to say when mail raises a request.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - a new mail raises a request with the right reporter and type;
  - an untrusted domain is refused;
  - an auto-reply is skipped;
  - a reply to an existing request is still a reply.
- **Browser:** the raised request in the customer's portal list.

issues.title: Send mail through an SMTP server that needs a login or implicit TLS
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want Armature to send through SES, Microsoft 365, Gmail or my company's relay, so that I do not have to run an open relay next to it.

## What happens today

`mail/mail.go:72` calls `smtp.SendMail(m.Addr, nil, ...)` with no authentication. The only setting is `ARMATURE_SMTP_ADDR` (`config/config.go:72,193`). POP3 already has a user, a password and TLS, but SMTP has none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ARMATURE_SMTP_USER`, `ARMATURE_SMTP_PASSWORD` and `ARMATURE_SMTP_TLS` (`starttls`, `implicit` or `none`). PLAIN auth is used only over TLS.
- [ ] The password comes from a secret in the chart, and the README's environment table lists all three.
- [ ] A refused login is logged once with a sentence, and the outbox keeps the mail for retry.

## Tests

- **Integration:** against the stack's Mailpit with auth required, or a small SMTP test server: a send with the login succeeds, and one with a wrong password fails with the logged sentence.

issues.title: Outgoing mail sends raw UTF-8 headers and does not thread with earlier mails about the same request
issues.body:
## What happens today

`mail/mail.go:55-63` writes `Subject` and `From` as raw UTF-8 (only stripped of control characters by `headerValue`), with no RFC 2047 encoding. The body has no `Content-Transfer-Encoding`. No message carries `In-Reply-To` or `References`, so mail clients do not group a request's mails.

**Scenario:**
- A request titled "Bestellung fur Muller" with umlauts, or in Japanese, arrives with a garbled subject at strict servers, or is refused by relays without SMTPUTF8.
- Each update on a request starts a new thread in the customer's mailbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-ASCII header values are encoded with `mime.QEncoding` (display names too). The body is sent quoted-printable or 8bit, declared.
- [ ] Mails about one request carry `References` and `In-Reply-To` pointing at a stable id for that request, for example the first notification's Message-ID derived from the key.
- [ ] Inbound matching keeps working with those headers.

## Tests

- **Unit:** a non-ASCII subject is encoded, and the thread headers are set.
- **Integration:** two mails about one request in Mailpit share a thread.

issues.title: Changing a request's priority or moving it to another project leaves its SLA clocks as they were
issues.body:
## What happens today

The issue Observer has no hook for updates (`issue/service.go:39-43`). The desk sets SLA goals from the request's policy when it is raised and moves clocks on transitions only. `issue/movecopy.go` leaves `sla_timer` rows in place when an issue moves.

**Scenario:**
- A request is raised as Low with a 3-day resolution goal, and an agent raises it to Critical, which should be 4 hours. The clock keeps the 3-day goal.
- A request moved to a project without the desk keeps its timers, which can still breach and notify.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A priority or request type change re-evaluates the matching policy and moves the open clocks to the new goal, keeping the time already run.
- [ ] Moving an issue out of a service project stops its clocks. Moving it into one starts the matching policy, or the move is refused. Pick one and write it down.
- [ ] The rule sits next to "The clocks move inside the issue's transaction".

## Tests

- **Integration:** the priority change, a move out, and a move in.

issues.title: A desk's business calendar accepts overlapping hours on a day and counts them twice
issues.body:
## What happens today

`desk/calendar.go:65-78` (`Validate`) checks that each span ends after it starts, but not that the spans of a day do not overlap. `WorkingDuration` (`:150-160`) adds every span, so the overlapping minutes count twice.

**Scenario:** Monday is entered as 09:00 to 13:00 and 12:00 to 17:00. The clock counts nine hours for Monday instead of eight, so goals run out an hour early.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Overlapping spans on one day are refused with a sentence naming them ("Monday: 12:00 to 17:00 overlaps 09:00 to 13:00; join them into one span").
- [ ] Calendars already saved with overlaps are counted with the overlap merged.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the refusal, and `WorkingDuration` over a merged pair.

issues.title: Let a desk's business calendar take its holidays from a holiday calendar
issues.body:
## User story

As a desk administrator, I want the SLA calendar to skip the same public holidays the organization already keeps, so that I maintain one list and the clocks agree with the plan.

## What happens today

`business_calendar.holidays` is a flat per-project list (`desk/calendar.go`), separate from the organization's holiday calendars (#28). The decision "Holidays are named calendars a person is given" names pointing the SLA calendar at a holiday calendar as later work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A business calendar can name a holiday calendar. Its days (half days as half the day's hours) are skipped by the clocks, alongside or instead of the desk's own list.
- [ ] Deleting a holiday calendar a desk uses is refused with a sentence naming the desk, or falls back to the desk's own list. Decide which.
- [ ] Changing the holiday calendar's days takes effect for open clocks from then on.

## Tests

- **Unit:** working time across a holiday taken from the named calendar.
- **Integration:** setting the link, a refusal for a non-administrator, and the clocks across a holiday.

issues.title: Group a desk's customers into customer organizations who can see each other's requests
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer at Globex, I want to see the requests my colleagues raised with the desk, so that we do not each report the same outage. As an agent, I want to see which company a request comes from.

## What happens today

There is no table or code for customer organizations. A customer sees their own requests and those they follow. Trusted domains decide who may write, not who may read together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A desk administrator can make customer organizations, add customers to them, and optionally add new customers by domain.
- [ ] A customer can choose to share a request with their organization when raising it, and can see the shared requests of their organization in the portal.
- [ ] Agents see the customer organization on the request, and queues and reports can filter by it.
- [ ] Internal notes stay invisible to every customer.
- [ ] The decisions and `docs/privacy.md` say who sees what.

## Tests

- **Integration:** sharing, visibility to a colleague, invisibility to another organization, notes still hidden, and RLS through raw SQL.
- **Browser:** a colleague sees the shared request in the portal.

issues.title: The rating link in the resolution mail goes to every follower and watching agent, not only the customer
issues.body:
## What happens today

`desk/mail.go:314-328` mints the one rating token ("the customer alone holds it") and sends the resolution mail with `n.tell`. `recipients` (`:206-229`) is the reporter plus everyone in `issue_watcher`, which includes followers and agents added by an @mention.

**Scenario:** an agent who was mentioned on the request, or a colleague of the customer who follows it, gets the same link and can rate before the customer does. The customer's own click then finds the rating already given.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The rating line goes only into the reporter's copy of the resolution mail. Everyone else gets the mail without it.
- [ ] The decision on ratings says who is asked.

## Tests

- **Integration:** a resolved request with a follower and a watching agent; only the reporter's mail in Mailpit holds `/rate/`.

issues.title: A CSV export holds at most 50 issues, not the 5000 it is meant to
issues.body:
## What happens today

`backend/internal/csvio/csvio.go:28` sets `ExportRows = 5000`, and `:62` calls `s.issues.List(ctx, filter, issue.Page{Limit: ExportRows, OrderBy: "key"})`. `issue/list.go:98` then does `if page.Limit <= 0 || page.Limit > 200 { page.Limit = 50 }`, so 5000 becomes 50. The search page reaches the export through `SavedFilterBar.tsx:115`.

**Scenario:** in a project with 300 issues, press Download CSV on the search page. The file holds a header and 50 rows, and nothing says it was cut.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The export reads up to `ExportRows`, paging through the list internally or with its own bound, without the API's page clamp.
- [ ] A result longer than `ExportRows` is refused, or cut with a final note row and a response header. Pick one.

## Tests

- **Integration:** export 120 issues and count 120 rows; the over-limit behaviour.

issues.title: Moving an epic to another project leaves its stories' subtasks behind, under a parent in the other project
issues.body:
## What happens today

`issue/movecopy.go:165-171` refuses to move a subtask or an issue with a parent, so an epic passes. Only its direct children are moved, by `SELECT c.id, c.key_num FROM issue c WHERE c.parent_id = $1` (`:231`).

The grandchildren are never updated, so `issue_hierarchy_guard` ("a parent has to be in the same project", `migrations/00005_issue_hierarchy.sql:89`) never runs for them. The children also skip the check that their status exists in the target workflow, and no history is written for them.

**Scenario:**
1. Epic A-1 has story A-2, which has subtask A-3.
2. Move A-1 to project B.

B-1 and B-2 are in B, while A-3 stays in A with its parent pointing at B-2. That breaks the same-project rule, and any later edit of A-3's parent or type hits the trigger.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Moving an issue moves its whole subtree, using a recursive query. Each row gets a new key, a status valid in its target workflow, and a history entry.
- [ ] The move is refused before anything changes if any descendant cannot move, with a sentence naming it.
- [ ] Old keys still find every moved issue.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - a three-level move, with keys, statuses, history and old-key lookups;
  - a refusal for a descendant whose type is missing in the target;
  - a raw SQL check that no parent ends up in another project.

issues.title: Moving an issue deletes its values for organization-wide fields, which still apply in the new project
issues.body:
## What happens today

`issue/movecopy.go:220` and `:254` run `DELETE FROM issue_field_value WHERE issue_id = $1` for every field. Organization fields have `project_id IS NULL` and apply in every project (`field/service.go` `Set`). The history written at `:283-300` mentions no custom field.

**Scenario:** set the organization field "Cost" to 120 on A-5, then move it to B. "Cost" is empty on B-9, and the changelog does not say it was cleared.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A move keeps the values of organization fields, and drops only those of the old project's own fields.
- [ ] Each dropped value is named in the move's history.
- [ ] The move dialog says which values will be dropped before the person confirms.

## Tests

- **Integration:** an organization field survives a move, and a project field's value is dropped with a history entry.

issues.title: Searching a custom field with ~ and a number or a date answers 500, and number comparisons can fail on a cast
issues.body:
## What happens today

`nql/compile.go:428-440` checks the literal's kind before the operator.
- A number builds `(v.value #>> '{}')::numeric ~ $n`, and a date builds `::date ~ $d`. Postgres has no such operators. That breaks the promise at `compile.go:66` that a compiled query cannot fail in the database.
- The guard `f.kind = 'number' AND (v.value #>> '{}')::numeric > $n` relies on `AND` being evaluated left to right, which Postgres does not promise. The cast refers only to `v`, so the planner can push it down to the scan of `issue_field_value`, where it meets text values.

`test/search_test.go` covers text fields only.

**Scenario:**
- `"Order ID" ~ 4711` answers 500 with "operator does not exist: numeric ~ double precision".
- `"Score" > 3` can raise "invalid input syntax for type numeric" when another project has a text field holding "high".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `~` and `!~` on a custom field always compare text, whatever the literal looks like. Or a number with `~` is a query error pointing at the operator.
- [ ] Number and date casts are guarded with `CASE WHEN f.kind = ... THEN ... END`, so they never meet another kind's value.
- [ ] Every NQL operator on a number and a date custom field compiles and runs.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the compiled SQL for each case.
- **Integration:** queries on number and date custom fields with every operator, next to a text field holding letters.

issues.title: Bulk edit reports an issue as left as it was after it already changed part of it
issues.body:
## What happens today

`bulk/bulk.go:35` says a refusal "is one issue that was left as it was", and the decision says "Bulk edit is one transaction per issue". In `one()` (`:91` onwards), `Update` (priority, assignee), `SetSprint`, `SetMilestone`, `SetTeam`, `SetIssueLabels` and `Transition` (`:154`) each run their own `s.db.Write`. A failure in a later step returns after the earlier ones have committed.

**Scenario:** bulk-apply priority High and the transition "Done" to an issue whose workflow does not offer Done. The dialog lists it as refused, but its priority is now High and its history says so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every change bulk edit makes to one issue happens in one transaction, through variants of the issue methods that take a transaction. A refusal leaves the issue as it was.
- [ ] Events and observers fire once per issue, inside that transaction.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the scenario above leaves priority and history unchanged; a raw count of history rows proves it.

issues.title: Changing an issue's type to one with another workflow resets its status without a record, and leaves it resolved
issues.body:
## What happens today

`issue/update.go:305-315` runs `UPDATE issue SET status_id = $2` to the new workflow's first status when the current one is not in it. The only change recorded is the type. There is no status change in the history, no `issue.transitioned` event, and `resolved_at` is never cleared. Reports and NQL `resolved` read `resolved_at` (`report/chart.go:71`, `report/flow.go:313`).

**Scenario:**
1. Bug X-4 is Done, with `resolved_at` set.
2. Change its type to Incident, whose workflow has no Done.

It now sits in Triage, while `resolved IS NOT EMPTY` and the throughput reports still count it as done. The history shows only the type change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A type change that moves the status records the status change and emits the transition event, so observers such as the SLA clocks see it.
- [ ] It clears `resolved_at` when the new status is not in the done category, and sets it when it is.
- [ ] Or the type change asks for the target status, as a move does with `ErrMoveNeedsStatus`. Pick one.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the scenario above, checking history, event, `resolved_at` and an NQL `resolved` query.

issues.title: Deleting a parent issue leaves its descendants' files in the bucket for good
issues.body:
## What happens today

`attachment/service.go:60-68` (`IssueDeleted`) leaves tombstones only for `attachment WHERE issue_id = $1`, the deleted issue itself. `issue/list.go:318` deletes the issue, and `parent_id ... ON DELETE CASCADE` takes its children and grandchildren with it. Their attachment rows cascade away without tombstones. The reaper works only from tombstones (`attachment/reaper.go:52`), and the decisions say the bucket is never listed.

**Scenario:** an epic has a story with a 20 MB attachment. Deleting the epic removes the story and its attachment row, but the object stays in storage with nothing pointing at it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deleting an issue leaves a tombstone for every attachment in its subtree, through a recursive query or an `AFTER DELETE` trigger on `attachment` that writes the tombstone.
- [ ] Other paths that remove attachment rows by cascade (project deletion, erasure) are covered by the same mechanism.

## Tests

- **Integration:** delete an epic whose story holds a file, see the tombstone, run the reaper, and see the object gone.

issues.title: text !~ "foo" and description !~ "foo" leave out every issue without a description
issues.body:
## What happens today

`nql/compile.go:350-364` builds `(summary ILIKE ... OR jsonb_to_tsvector('simple', i.description, ...) @@ ...)`, and `:160` negates it as `NOT (...)`. `jsonb_to_tsvector(NULL)` is NULL, so `false OR NULL` is NULL, and `NOT NULL` drops the row. An emptied description is stored as NULL.

**Scenario:** P-1 has the summary "Login page" and no description. `text !~ "payment"` does not return it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Negated text tests treat a missing description as not matching, so they include such issues (wrap the test in `COALESCE(..., false)`).
- [ ] Every negated operator over a nullable column is checked for the same pattern, and an issue with the column empty is counted on the side the reader expects.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the compiled SQL.
- **Integration:** `text !~` and `description !~` include an issue with no description.

issues.title: An issue moved twice can no longer be found by its first key
issues.body:
## What happens today

`issue/movecopy.go:226` and `:259` set `moved_from` to the current key, overwriting the one before. `ByOldKey` (`:311`) matches only `WHERE i.moved_from = $1`. The decisions promise that the old key stays, so "the address that was mailed around still finds it".

**Scenario:** move A-1 to B (B-5), then B-5 to C (C-2). `/issues/A-1` answers 404.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every key an issue has had finds it, for example from a table `issue_old_key (org_id, issue_id, key)`, unique per organization, with RLS.
- [ ] Existing `moved_from` values are carried into it by a migration.
- [ ] Old-key lookups across the API, the SPA's redirects and mail matching use it.

## Tests

- **Integration:** two moves, then both old keys open the issue; a raw SQL check of the uniqueness and the tenant policy.

issues.title: When two people edit an issue at once, the later save silently wins
issues.body:
## What happens today

`issue/update.go` (`Update`) writes the fields given, for example `UPDATE issue SET description = $2`, without comparing against what the editor read. There is no ETag, If-Match or expected `updatedAt` anywhere in `backend/internal` or `web/src`. `web/src/features/issues/Description.tsx:13` sends only `{description: draft}`. A save with no change also records "updated the description" again.

**Scenario:**
1. Two tabs open the description editor.
2. Tab A saves.
3. Tab B saves its stale draft, and A's text is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An edit of the description (and of the summary) carries the `updatedAt` it started from. On a mismatch the API answers 409: "Somebody changed this issue since you opened it. Reload it and apply your edit again."
- [ ] The SPA keeps the person's draft on a 409 and shows the newer text beside it.
- [ ] A save that changes nothing records nothing.
- [ ] `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the stale save is refused with 409, a fresh one succeeds, and a no-op save writes no history.
- **Vitest:** the draft survives a 409.

issues.title: Search results and the project's issue list cannot be paged past the first 100
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working through a query that matches 450 issues, I want to page through all of them, so that the ones after the first 100 are not out of reach.

## What happens today

- `web/src/routes/search.tsx:29` calls `useIssues({ q, limit: SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE })` (100, `config.ts:140`) with no offset. `:70` says "N issues, the first 100 shown".
- `routes/project-detail.tsx:34,59` caps at `ISSUE_PAGE_SIZE` (100), while `:179` shows the full total, with nothing saying rows are missing.
- The API accepts `offset` (`httpapi/filter_handlers.go:172`), but no `.tsx` uses it.
- The CSV export is no way out either, while it is capped at 50 (#80).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both lists page (or load more) through `offset` and `total`, with the page kept in the URL.
- [ ] The project page says how many of the total are shown.
- [ ] Bulk selection says whether it covers the shown page or the whole result.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** paging controls and the URL.
- **Browser:** page to the second hundred of a seeded result.

issues.title: Bulk edit can move, delete, remove labels and set versions, components and fields
issues.body:
## User story

As a project administrator reorganising work, I want to move 80 issues to a new project, or strip a retired label from them, in one step and not 80.

## What happens today

- `bulk/bulk.go:22-32` `Input` holds only Priority, Assignee, SprintID, MilestoneID, TeamID, AddLabels and Transition.
- `web/src/features/filters/BulkBar.tsx` offers priority, assignee, add labels and a free-text transition name only. It does not offer the sprint, milestone and team changes the API supports.
- Move exists only one issue at a time (`POST /issues/{key}/move`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bulk input gains `moveTo` (project, with a status mapping), `removeLabels`, `fixVersions`, `components`, custom field values and `delete`. Each goes through the existing per-issue service calls, one transaction per issue.
- [ ] BulkBar offers sprint, milestone and team pickers, and picks the transition from the names the selected issues share.
- [ ] Delete confirms with the count and the noun ("Delete 80 issues").
- [ ] Each operation is checked against the caller's permissions per issue, and refused issues are listed with their reason.

## Tests

- **Integration:** each new operation, with a refusal per permission.
- **Vitest:** the new pickers.
- **Browser:** bulk-remove a label from a search result.

issues.title: Three small edges in search, import and labels: ILIKE wildcards, a BOM before a quoted header, and coining the same label twice
issues.body:
## What happens today

- **Wildcards:** `summary ~ "50%"` passes `%` and `_` straight into ILIKE (`nql/compile.go:353`), so it matches any "50".
- **BOM:** `csvio/mapping.go:87` strips the byte order mark only after parsing. A file that starts with a BOM followed by a quoted header (`"Summary",...`), as Excel writes it, fails with "bare \" in non-quoted field".
- **Labels:** `label.SetIssueLabels` coins a new label with a plain `INSERT` (`label/label.go:265`). Two people tagging with the same new word at the same moment make one request fail with a unique violation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Text searches escape `%`, `_` and `\` before ILIKE.
- [ ] The import strips a leading BOM before the CSV reader sees the bytes.
- [ ] Coining a label is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (org_id, lower(name)) DO NOTHING`, then read, so both requests succeed with the same label.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the escaped pattern, and a BOM with a quoted header.
- **Integration:** two concurrent label coinings both succeed.

issues.title: The worker acknowledges events it failed to handle and never re-reads pending ones, so audit, mail, webhooks and rules are lost
issues.body:
## What happens today

Every stream consumer follows the same pattern: `err := X.Handle(...)`, log a warning, then `XAck` anyway:
- `audit/audit.go:305-316`
- `notify/fanout.go:66-76`
- `webhook/consumer.go:60-70`
- `automation/consumer.go:58-68`
- `desk/mail.go:157-167`

Every `XReadGroup` reads only `">"`. Nothing reads the group's pending list (`0`), and there is no `XAUTOCLAIM`. On SIGTERM the context is cancelled, so the rest of a batch of 50 fails both `Handle` and `XAck` and stays pending for good.

The relay's at-least-once promise ("A transactional outbox rather than publishing events directly") therefore ends at Redis.
