issues.title: Keep what is typed in project settings when the project refetches, and click a button only once it is enabled
issues.body:
## What happens

The browser scenario "a project's sidebar links to its documentation" fails now and then (twice in a row on one branch, once on another, and alone with ONLY): the last save, which clears the link, never reaches the api.

Two things meet there:

- `useUpdateProject` stays pending until every project query has refetched, so "Save changes" keeps its spinner and is disabled after the sidebar already shows the saved link. `clickButton` in `e2e/helpers.mjs` clicks the first button with the label without checking that it is enabled, so a click on the busy button does nothing and the scenario waits for a save that never happens.
- `routes/project-settings.tsx` copies the project into the form on every change of the query's data. When the refetch lands after somebody has started typing, what they typed is replaced by what the server had.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `clickButton` waits for an enabled button with the label, as a person waits for the spinner, and fails with a sentence when none becomes enabled
- [ ] The project settings form keeps what somebody typed when the project refetches; a field nobody touched follows the server
- [ ] The documentation scenario passes repeatedly under a full parallel run

## Tests

Vitest: a refetch with new data after typing leaves the typed value. Browser: the full suite, and the scenario several times on its own.

issues.title: Wait for the replica before reading another session's write in two integration tests
issues.body:
## What happens

Two integration tests fail now and then in a full run and pass alone (8 of 8 each):

- `TestAnAbsenceIsWrittenByThePersonAndByThoseWhoPlanWithThem`: a colleague lists absences right after Ada records hers, and Ada's half day is missing (failed in 2 of the last 3 full runs on main, and on #242's branch).
- `TestADeskTrustsDomainsNotAddresses`: a customer lists the portal's desks right after the owner narrowed one desk's trusted domains, and still sees it.

Both read in one session what another session has just written. A session waits for the replica only for its own writes, so under a loaded full run the second session can read from a replica that has not caught up. The harness already has `h.waitForPrimary` for this case ("what a client that reads from the replica needs after somebody else's write about it"); these two tests do not call it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both tests wait for the replica before a session reads what another session wrote
- [ ] The full integration suite passes several runs in a row

issues.title: Page the projects list, so thousands of projects keep the page and the sidebar fast
issues.body:
## What happens

The projects page draws every project the reader may see, in one list. On the shared development installation that is 5314 projects, all left behind by browser runs, since every scenario makes its own and none is removed.

- `GET /api/v1/projects` answers in 0.2s, but with 3.2 MB of JSON (`project.Service.List` has no limit, `backend/internal/project/service.go:243`).
- `routes/projects.tsx` renders one `ProjectRow`, with its menu, per project.
- On a loaded machine the page takes longer than the browser suite's 15s wait. Four scenarios in `e2e/scenarios/projects.mjs` that open `/projects` failed together in the full runs of #253 and #259:
  - "a project can be created and is listed"
  - "a project made from the Scrum template shows only the running sprint"
  - "the Task tracking template gives a project a simple workflow of its own"
  - "a project posts a status update and the projects table shows it"
- Each passes when run alone, in 7s to 14s, which is already close to the limit and grows with every run.

The same list is loaded by the sidebar (`features/shell/Sidebar.tsx`), so every page of the app fetches all 3.2 MB on load. It is also loaded by the command palette, the create issue dialog, the overview, the role table, clone and move, and the tokens page. An installation with a few thousand real projects would see all of these slow down.

## What to do

- **Page the list on the server:** `GET /projects` takes a limit and an offset, or a cursor, and a text filter over the key and the name. It answers with the total, as the issue search does.
- **Page the list in the web:** the projects page shows one page at a time, keeps the page and the filter in the address, and offers a search box.
- **Other callers:** callers that need every project, such as pickers, either page through the list or use a lighter endpoint. Check each caller of `useProjects`.
- **Browser suite:** the scenarios find their own project through the filter, not by reading the whole page.

## Done when

- The projects page stays fast with thousands of projects.
- The four scenarios pass in a full run on the shared installation as it is.

issues.title: The search page shows every shared search as a chip, so a few dozen push the results out of reach
issues.body:
## What happens

The row of saved searches on the search page (`web/src/features/filters/SavedFilterBar.tsx`) draws a chip for every saved search the reader can see. That includes every search anyone in the installation shared.

On the shared development installation there are 39 shared "Open work ..." searches, one left by each run of "a search is saved, starred and offered on the search page" (`e2e/scenarios/work.mjs:200`). Their chips fill about ten lines above the results.

The browser scenario "one issue is exported from its page, ticked rows from search..." now fails even when run alone. The second result row sits under the bulk bar, which sticks to the bottom of the screen, and the click on its box lands on the bar. That scenario failed in the full browser run of #260 on top of main.

An installation where people share a few dozen searches would see the same wall of chips.

## What to do

- The row offers as chips only:
  - the reader's starred searches;
  - their own searches;
  - the search that is running.
- Everything else stays on the All saved searches page, which already lists and stars them.
- The rule is a pure function beside `orderFilters`, with a unit test.

## Done when

- A shared search by someone else does not appear on the search page until the reader stars it.
- The export scenario passes on the shared installation as it is.

issues.title: On a database migrated as a plain owner, 00911 fails: planning_method contains null values
issues.body:
## What happens today

`project` forces row level security on its owner, and the chart migrates as an owner that is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS. `00911_resource_planning.sql` backfills `planning_method` with `UPDATE project ...` without lifting it, so the owner sees no project and fills none. The following `SET NOT NULL` then refuses the upgrade:

```
ERROR 00911_resource_planning.sql: ... ERROR: column "planning_method" of relation "project" contains null values (SQLSTATE 23502)
```

The second backfill in the same file, which turns the resources page on for software projects, would quietly add it to none.

`backend/test/owner_migrate_test.go` migrates as such an owner, but its database holds no project, so it passes.

**Scenario:** a chart deployment with existing projects upgrades past 00910. The migration fails, and the installation stays at 00910.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 00911 lifts row security on `project` and `board` around its backfills and forces it again after them, as 00904 and 00916 do.
- [ ] `owner_migrate_test.go` writes a project with a scrum board and one without before 00911, and expects `scrum` and `kanban` with the resources page on.
- [ ] Both tables force row security again after the migrations.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the extended owner-migration test fails with the error above without the change.

issues.title: Dialogs and popovers taller than the screen cannot be scrolled, so their buttons are out of reach
issues.body:
## What happens

When a dialog is taller than the window, its lower part cannot be reached. With the built-in arrangement, the new issue dialog asks for about fifteen fields plus every custom field, so on a laptop screen the footer with "Create issue" sits below the window and nothing scrolls.

**Why:**
- In `web/src/components/ui/Dialog.tsx:35-45`, the backdrop is `fixed inset-0 ... items-start pt-[12vh]`. It has no `overflow-y-auto`, and the panel has no `max-h`.
- `useScrollLock` (`web/src/components/ui/overlay.ts:107-117`) sets `body { overflow: hidden }` while a dialog is open.
- A fixed box is not a scroll container, so the overflow is simply lost. Tab cannot reach the hidden controls either.

The browser suite never noticed, because `clickButton` (`e2e/helpers.mjs:754-764`) clicks through the DOM and works on buttons outside the viewport.

**Dialogs that grow past the screen in the same way:**
- the new issue dialog (`features/issues/CreateIssueDialog.tsx`);
- the automation rule editor, one block per condition and action (`features/automation/RuleEditor.tsx`);
- the bulk edit result, one row per refused issue, up to 200 (`features/filters/BulkBar.tsx:107`);
- a project's status history, every update ever posted (`features/projects/StatusStrip.tsx:117`);
- the export columns, the dashboard share links, the absence editor, and the move dialog.

**Menus and popovers:**
- `Menu` (`components/ui/Menu.tsx:104`) and `Popover` (`components/ui/Popover.tsx:41`) have no height limit.
- `useAnchored` (`overlay.ts:126-178`) clamps the position to the viewport but never the height.
- **Affected:** the sidebar project switcher, which holds 20 projects and a filter box, so its last projects are cut off on a 768px screen. Also the fix-version, affects-version and component pickers (`features/versions/IssueVersionFields.tsx:49`), the board's quick filters (`features/board/QuickFilters.tsx:149`), the resource grid's week popover (`features/resources/ResourceGrid.tsx:114`), and the canned responses menu (`features/issues/IssueActivity.tsx:201`).

**Errors out of view:** the create dialog (`CreateIssueDialog.tsx:109-110`) and the rule editor (`RuleEditor.tsx:80`) show their error at the top of the body, while the button that caused it is in the footer. Once the body scrolls, pressing Create seems to do nothing.

## What to do

- **Dialog:**
  - the panel becomes a column with a height limit;
  - the header and footer always show, and the body scrolls (the `Drawer` pattern, `Dialog.tsx:153`);
  - the top offset and margins become constants in `web/src/config.ts`.
- **Menus and popovers:** `useAnchored` also gives the height available on the side the panel opens to. Menu, Popover and the mention lists cap themselves to it and scroll.
- **Errors:** they show directly above the footer and are scrolled into view.

## Done when

- At a 1280x600 window, the new issue dialog's Create button is on screen and works by a real click, and the body scrolls to its last field.
- The project switcher reaches its last project.

issues.title: Label fields show every label in the installation instead of suggesting matches as you type
issues.body:
## What happens

Labels are shared by every project in the installation, and every label field loads all of them. `GET /labels` takes no search and no limit (`backend/internal/httpapi/label_handlers.go:13-20`, `backend/internal/label/label.go:101-121`).

**Where it shows:**
- **New issue dialog** (`web/src/features/issues/create/controls.tsx:65-97`): below the input, every label in the installation is drawn as a chip under "Labels already in use". With a few hundred labels the field is a wall of chips.
- **Issue page** (`web/src/features/labels/LabelPicker.tsx:18,64-68`): every label goes into a native `<datalist>`, which the browser lists in full on focus.
- **Project issue list** (`web/src/routes/project-detail.tsx:186-195`): "Filter by label" is a select of every label in the installation, from all projects.
- **Bulk edit** "Add labels" (`web/src/features/filters/BulkBar.tsx:64`) and the rule editor's "Add a label" action (`web/src/features/automation/RuleEditor.tsx:189`) are free text, with no suggestions, so a typo makes a new label.

## What to do

- **Server:** `GET /labels` takes `q` and `limit`. Names starting with the text come first, then names containing it. With neither given, it answers as today, for the labels settings page.
- **One shared input:** a text box that shows nothing until you type, then suggests matching existing labels and offers to create the typed word. Arrow keys move through the suggestions; Enter or a comma adds one; Backspace on an empty box removes the last label added.
- **Where it goes:** the new issue dialog, the issue page, bulk edit's "Add labels", the rule editor's label action, and the project issue list's label filter.
- **Out of scope:** removing labels in bulk is part of #91.

## Done when

- No field draws labels nobody asked for.
- Typing the start of an existing label suggests it, and choosing it adds it.

issues.title: People pickers and lists load and draw every member of the installation
issues.body:
## What happens

Every place that picks a person loads every member of the installation and renders them all. `/members` and `/users` take no search and no limit (`backend/internal/httpapi/meta_handlers.go:143-150`). The shared development installation already holds thousands of accounts from test runs.

**Native selects listing every member:**

| Picker | Location |
|---|---|
| Assignee and reporter | `features/issues/PeopleFields.tsx:18-22, 42-46` |
| The new issue dialog's assignee and reporter | `features/issues/create/controls.tsx:16-24` |
| Watchers | `features/issues/WatchersPanel.tsx:59-64` |
| Bulk assignee | `features/filters/BulkBar.tsx:56-60` |
| Component lead and default assignee | `features/versions/ComponentList.tsx:76-86` |
| A role grant's "Who" (members and every group) | `features/access/RoleTable.tsx:95-135` |
| "Add somebody" on every group card | `features/access/GroupList.tsx:51-125` |
| "Add somebody" on every team card | `features/teams/TeamList.tsx:98-185` |
| Project lead | `routes/project-settings.tsx:103-108` |

**Worst case:** the import's people mapping (`features/import/PeopleCard.tsx:54`) gives each person in the file a select of every member. 50 names against 6000 members is 300,000 options, and the page hangs.

**Lists with no paging or search:** the Users page (`features/users/UserTable.tsx:64`) and the Access page's member list (`features/access/MemberList.tsx:26`).

## What to do

- **Server:** `/members` and `/users` take `q` and `limit`, as `/projects` does since #261.
- **One shared person picker** that searches as you type, in the style of `features/projects/ProjectPicker.tsx`, used everywhere above.

issues.title: The app is wider than a phone's screen in headers, toolbars, tabs, tables and the sidebar
issues.milestone: One look with Stator and Exciter
issues.body:
## What happens

At phone width (375px) several parts of the app are wider than the screen, so the page scrolls sideways or loses content.

**Headers:**
- **Portal header** (`web/src/routes/app.tsx:145`): a fixed-height row that never wraps, holding the installation name, two links, the email (`:154`, not truncated) and the avatar, about 600px in all. The email and account menu end up off-screen.

**Rows of buttons and tabs that cannot wrap:**
- Page header actions (`components/ui/PageHeader.tsx:70`, `shrink-0`). The dashboard's four buttons come to about 440px.
- Toolbar end buttons (`components/ui/Toolbar.tsx:9`). The bulk bar's three buttons come to about 310px.
- The issue header's transitions (`features/issues/IssueHeader.tsx:134`, `shrink-0`). A transition error widens the whole header.
- Tabs (`components/ui/Tabs.tsx:23`), with no horizontal scroll. Access has five.

**Tables:** the summary cell is `max-w-0 truncate` beside fixed-width columns (`features/issues/IssueTable.tsx:82`, `routes/portal.tsx:166`, `routes/queues.tsx:113`). On a phone it shrinks to nothing, so a customer sees their requests without their text.

**Layout:**
- The expanded sidebar stays a 232px column beside the rail (`features/shell/Sidebar.tsx:99`), leaving about 95px for the page.
- Page padding is a fixed `px-8` at every width (`routes/app.tsx:104,106,161`, `IssueHeader.tsx:13`).
- The search page's sticky bulk bar (`routes/search.tsx:95`) wraps to four or five rows pinned over the results.
- Chips never truncate (`components/ui/Chip.tsx`), so a long epic name runs out of the quick-filter popover.

## What to do

- The headers, button rows and tabs wrap or scroll.
- Summary cells keep a minimum width, or the fixed columns hide below `sm`.
- Below the rail breakpoint the sidebar opens as an overlay.
- Padding is smaller on phones.
- On phones the bulk bar collapses to a count and one button.
- Chips truncate.
- A browser scenario at 375px checks for no horizontal scroll on the main pages.

issues.title: Administration lists load every workflow, scheme, role grant and label in the installation
issues.body:
## What happens

Administration pages load and draw everything in the installation, and the browser runs keep adding to it:
- **Workflows and schemes:**
  - a workflow select per issue type, each listing every workflow (`web/src/features/workflows/ProjectWorkflows.tsx:166`);
  - the scheme select (`:241`);

## What to do

- **Pickers:** a searching picker instead of the full selects.

issues.title: The swimlane editor offers every status in the installation, not the project's
issues.body:
## What happens

The swimlane editor (`web/src/features/board/SwimlaneEditor.tsx:284`) gives each lane a checkbox for every status in the installation (`/statuses`), not only the statuses of the project's workflows.

Its warning "N states not on the board (...)" (`:83`) also counts and lists every status the board does not use, including other projects' statuses. So it always reports states that cannot reach the board.

## What to do

- The editor offers only the statuses of the workflows the project's scheme maps.
- The warning counts only those.

issues.title: Errors on long pages appear far from the button that caused them
issues.body:
## What happens

On long pages, the error from an action shows at the top of the page while the button that caused it is far below:
- **Portal "Raise a request"** (`web/src/routes/portal.tsx:272`): the error is above the article search, the request types, the details and the files. "Send request" is at `:380`, so on a phone the error is a screen away.
- **Users page** (`features/users/UserTable.tsx:50-51`): errors from deactivating someone or removing their second factor appear above a table of every account. Acting on a row far down shows nothing nearby.
- **Labels page** (`routes/labels.tsx:40`): the same, above the full label table.
- **Project settings** (`routes/project-settings.tsx:96`): the error is above the form while Save is below it. This one matters only on a phone.

## What to do

- Show the error next to the button, or on the row that was acted on.
- Or use a toast, and scroll the error into view when it appears.

issues.title: Let a person ask for access to an issue they may not see, without telling whether it exists
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter show Armature issues on their pages with each reader's own token. A reader who may not see an issue gets 404, the same answer as for an issue that does not exist, so the page can only say "you may not see PROJ-12, or it does not exist". People take that for a fault. (Stator: praetorianer777/Stator#426.)

Armature treats existence as privileged (`httpapi/errors.go`, `scope.go`), and that should stay the default. Two ways to help the reader without weakening it:

**1. Ask for access, without learning anything (recommended)**
- `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/access-requests` with an optional message. It always answers `202 Accepted` with the same body, whether the issue exists, the caller may already see it, or the project is hidden from them; so it reveals nothing.
- When the issue exists and the caller may not see it, the project's administrators get a notification (in Armature and by mail) naming the caller, the key and the message, with a one-click way to grant access to the issue's project. Repeated requests by one person for one project within a day are folded into one.
- Rate limited per caller.
- Partners link to it: Stator's "You may not see PROJ-12, or it no longer exists. Ask for access" calls it with the reader's token.
- Capability `issue.access-requests@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.

**2. Optionally say "restricted" for projects that allow it**
- A per-project setting, off by default: "Show that issues exist to people who may not see them". When on, a caller who may not see an issue of that project gets `403` with code `not_permitted` and the project's name, instead of `404`.
- Only the project's administrators can turn it on; the settings page says what it reveals. Projects that must stay hidden keep the 404.

Both covered by tests that a caller cannot tell apart an existing hidden issue from a missing one unless the project opted in.

https://claude.ai/code/session_012upyidVTNM6iSeHELAc2fy

issues.title: Let partner tools get a person's token in one click, with consent
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter call Armature as each person, with a personal access token the person makes in Armature and pastes into the other tool. Many people give up at that step. A partner should be able to get that token in one click, with the person's consent.

- Armature acts as an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for partner tools: authorization code flow with PKCE, refresh tokens, revocation (RFC 7009).
- Clients are registered by an Armature administrator (name, redirect URIs, allowed scopes), or by the partner during the administrator's connect step (see the webhook issue); a registered client shows its name on the consent page.
- Consent page: "**Stator** wants to read issues and link pages as **<person>**: [Allow] [Cancel]", listing the scopes in words.
- Scopes map to what a personal access token can do today (read, issue.write, issue.transition, comment.write, remote links), and the issued token never exceeds the person's own rights.
- Issued tokens appear in the person's token list as "Stator (connected app)", revocable there; revoking ends the refresh token too.
- Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and the capability `oauth.partner-tokens@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.
- With a shared Keycloak realm, Armature accepts Keycloak token exchange (RFC 8693) for a partner client as an alternative, so a signed-in person needs no click at all; documented as optional.

Partners: praetorianer777/Stator and Cloudster1/Exciter use it for their "Connect Armature" button.

https://claude.ai/code/session_012upyidVTNM6iSeHELAc2fy

issues.title: Let a partner tool create its own webhook once an administrator agrees
issues.body:
Connecting a partner (Stator, Exciter) today means an Armature administrator adds a webhook by hand, picks the topics and copies a secret into the partner. A partner should be able to set up its own webhook once an Armature administrator agrees.

- `POST /api/v1/webhooks/partner` (or part of the OAuth consent for an administrator, scope `webhooks.manage`): the partner names its receiver URL and topics; Armature creates the endpoint, owned by the partner client, and returns the secret once.
- The administrator sees and can remove it in the webhook list, marked with the partner's name; the partner can rotate its secret and change its topics, never other endpoints.
- Armature's outbound guard still applies; if the receiver is refused, the answer says which value to add to `network.outboundAllow`.
- Capability `webhooks.partner@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.

issues.title: Typing a space in the project switcher's filter box closes the menu
issues.body:
## What happens

In the sidebar's project switcher, typing a space into the "Filter projects" box closes the menu. You cannot filter by a project name with two words, such as "Customer Portal". A probe in the browser suite showed the menu open before the space and gone after it.

## Why

The filter box is the label of a menu item (`web/src/features/shell/Sidebar.tsx:236-242`), so the `<input>` sits inside the item's `<button>`. An input inside a button is not valid HTML. The browser treats Space as activating the button, which picks the item and closes the menu. The handlers `onKeyDown` and `onClick` both call `stopPropagation`, which stops neither.

## What to do

- Render the filter box outside the menu's items, for example as a header slot of `Menu` (`web/src/components/ui/Menu.tsx`), so it is a plain input in the menu panel.
- Arrow Down from the box moves into the list.
- A browser scenario types a two-word name into the box and sees the matching project with the menu still open.

issues.title: Offer webhook envelope version 2 in the CloudEvents shape
issues.body:
Armature, Stator and Exciter send webhooks in one shared envelope, version 1: `{version, id, topic, occurredAt, payload}` plus `source`. Version 2 follows the CloudEvents 1.0 specification, so any receiver, a future relay in Dynamo, or a standard broker understands it without tool-specific code.

- Structured mode (`application/cloudevents+json`): `specversion: "1.0"`, `id`, `source` (e.g. `/armature`, `/stator`, `/exciter`, or the instance's URL), `type` (e.g. `dev.armature.issue.updated`, `dev.stator.page.remote_link.removed`), `time`, `datacontenttype: "application/json"`, `data` (the version 1 payload), and the extension attribute `dataversion` for the payload's own version.
- Signatures stay as in version 1 (HMAC over the body, timestamped signature header), since CloudEvents leaves authentication to the transport.
- An endpoint chooses the version it receives when it is registered; version 1 stays the default and keeps working for at least one Dynamo release after version 2 ships. The receiver side accepts both.
- Event types are listed with their payloads in the tool's OpenAPI document (or a schema beside it) and in Dynamo's shared list (praetorianer777/Dynamo#4).
- Events stay thin: ids, keys and what changed, no content a subscriber's own rights might not cover.
- Capability `webhooks@2` in `/api/v1/meta` once supported, next to `webhooks@1`.

https://claude.ai/code/session_012upyidVTNM6iSeHELAc2fy

issues.title: Give portal answers a shape of their own, with what a customer reads
issues.body:
## What to do

The portal answers with a shape of its own, holding what a customer reads, instead of the issue the agents work on:

- **A request:** key, summary, description, status and its category, priority, request type, company and whether it is shared with the company, the dates, and the number of comments the customer can read.
- **People:** assignee, reporter, comment authors and uploaders appear as id, name and avatar.
- **Comments and attachments:** the public ones, in the same shape.
- **Followers:** the reporter sees the addresses of the people they added; anyone else on the list appears by name.

This covers request detail, the request lists, raising a request, replies and attachments. A contract test checks that each portal answer carries exactly these fields.

issues.title: Saving a workflow reads the statuses of every project in the installation
issues.body:
## What happens

Saving a workflow reads the statuses of every active project in the installation, one query per project, even when the save added no status and even for projects that never use the workflow.

`board.Follower.WorkflowSaved` (`backend/internal/board/follow.go:22-56`):
- selects every project with `archived_at IS NULL`;
- calls `workflow.Store.ProjectStatuses` for each of them, inside the workflow's own transaction;
- only then checks whether any status in `added` is reachable.

It does not return early when `added` is empty, and it does not narrow to projects whose scheme maps this workflow. The comment above it says a read per project "an administrator saving a workflow can afford". On the shared development installation, with thousands of projects, saving the default workflow takes about 9 to 15 seconds. That makes the serial designer scenario "a status coined in the designer..." (`e2e/scenarios/dashboards.mjs`) and `TestALaneForAStatusAddedToTheWorkflowCanBeMovedOffTheEnd` time out under load.

## What to do

- Return straight away when `added` is empty.
- Otherwise find, in one query, the projects whose scheme maps this workflow for some issue type (the default scheme counts for projects without one), and read statuses only for those.
- Keep the test that a board grows a lane for an added status, and add one that a save which adds nothing touches no board.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Fcm9MLcqYqWHeiKXeXAmkV

issues.title: Match the start of words in issue descriptions with text ~
issues.body:
`text ~ "meta"` does not find an issue whose description says "metadata". In `backend/internal/nql/compile.go` the summary part matches any part of a word (`i.summary ILIKE '%' || $n || '%'`), but the description part needs whole words: `jsonb_to_tsvector('simple', i.description, '["string"]') @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $n)`. People searching as they type (Stator's issue search, praetorianer777/Stator#425) type the start of a word and expect it to match.

- Let `text ~` match the start of each word in the description too: build the tsquery from the typed words as prefixes, `word1:* & word2:*`. Build it from tokens Armature extracts itself, e.g. `to_tsvector('simple', $n)` lexemes joined with `:* &`, or strip everything but letters and digits from each word before appending `:*`, so the text never reaches `to_tsquery` as query syntax.
- `summary ~` stays a substring match; `description ~` (if it exists) gets the same prefix rule as `text ~`.
- Keep the index use in mind: a prefix tsquery still uses a GIN index on the description's tsvector, if there is one; if there is none, consider adding it.
- Tests: `text ~ meta` finds "metadata" in a description, `text ~ "data meta"` finds "metadata about data", and characters like `& | ! : * ( )` in the typed text are plain characters, never operators.

issues.title: The create issue dialog cannot scroll with many labels, hiding Create
issues.body:
Creating an issue when many labels (tags) are set or offered: the "Create issue" dialog grows past the bottom of the window, cannot be scrolled, and its Create button is out of reach, so the issue cannot be created.

Reported by a user of a deployed Armature (desktop browser).

**Steps:**
1. Have a project with many labels (a few dozen).
2. Open "Create issue" and add many labels, or open the label field so its list shows.
3. The dialog extends below the window; scrolling the page or the dialog does not reveal the footer with Create.

**Expected:** the dialog never exceeds the window; its body scrolls while the header and the footer with Create and Cancel stay visible; a long label list scrolls inside its own popover (or the chosen labels wrap within a bounded, scrollable area) instead of stretching the dialog.

**Where to look:** `web/src/features/issues/CreateIssueDialog.tsx` and `web/src/components/ui/Dialog.tsx` (the body has `min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`, so something in the create dialog likely escapes it: a container without `min-h-0`, a fixed height, or the label picker rendered inline rather than as a popover).

**Tests:** a browser test with, say, 60 labels in a project and 30 chosen, at desktop and mobile size, that scrolls to and clicks Create; an accessibility check that Create is reachable by keyboard.

issues.title: test(theme): import Exciter's exported theme file, so the three products' themes stay one family
issues.milestone: One look with Stator and Exciter
issues.body:
Exciter, Armature and Stator share one theme file format, `armature-theme/1`, so a theme made in any of the three should import unchanged into the other two (Cloudster1/Exciter#59).

On Exciter's side, `backend/internal/theme/testdata` now holds themes exported from a running Armature and a running Stator, each made with a file of its own. Each imports into Exciter and exports again the same. Exciter's own export is committed beside them as `exciter.armature-theme.json`, and an Exciter integration test keeps it current.

**Asked of Armature**
- Vendor Exciter's `backend/internal/theme/testdata/exciter.armature-theme.json` byte for byte from Exciter's `main`, once Cloudster1/Exciter#59 is merged, and pin it by its SHA-256 the way the example themes are pinned.
- In a test, import it, export it again, and compare: the same name, spec and files, with each file id replaced by the file's place in the list. This is how Exciter's `backend/test/theme_exchange_test.go` compares, and it trims the CSS as all three products do when they save.
- Exciter also vendors the token names of Armature's `web/src/lib/theme-tokens.ts` (`make theme-tokens`). A rename here shows up there as a failing test, so a renamed token is worth a note to Exciter.

The three products share the same 44 tokens today. A token added later travels through the others because each keeps any well-formed name and draws only what its own stylesheet has.

issues.title: A token exchange or a narrower consent drops a connected app's webhook scope
issues.body:
Since #296 and #297, a person has one grant per connected app, and a new grant replaces the old one's scopes (`grant()` upserts on `(user_id, client_id)`). Two paths give a narrower grant than the one a person already holds:

- The token exchange from a Keycloak token (`fromIdentityProvider`) never gives `webhooks.partner`, so it replaces an administrator's grant that held it.
- A later consent that asks for fewer scopes replaces the grant the same way.

What happens: an Armature administrator connects Stator with `webhooks.partner`, and Stator sets up its webhook. Later the same administrator signs in to Stator, and Stator trades their Keycloak token for a grant (Stator #430). Their grant now lacks `webhooks.partner` and its old refresh token has ended, so Stator can no longer change, rotate, test or recreate its own webhook until somebody connects it as an administrator again.

Asked: an exchange or consent keeps the scopes the existing grant already holds that the new request did not ask to drop, or at least keeps `webhooks.partner`. Alternatively, docs/oauth.md says that a new grant replaces the scopes, so partners ask for the union themselves.

Stator works around it meanwhile by exchanging only when it holds no grant for the person, and by asking an administrator for every scope at once.

issues.title: Add a suite demo filled with the issues of Armature, Exciter and Stator
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Armature together with Exciter and Stator, I want a demo whose issues are the suite's own development history, so that I see the three tools working on real, linked content rather than invented examples.

Part of one suite demo: Armature holds the issues, Stator the documentation (praetorianer777/Stator#457) and Exciter the requirements (Cloudster1/Exciter#270), and Exciter traces between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Adding it:** an administrator adds the suite demo once, from Settings > Installation beside "Add the demo project", and `make seed` adds it too. It is refused when one of its keys is taken.
- [ ] **Projects:** three projects, `ARM`, `EXC` and `STA`, hold the GitHub issues of `Cloudster1/Armature`, `Cloudster1/Exciter` and `praetorianer777/Stator`. Pull requests are left out.
- [ ] **Issues:** each keeps its GitHub number as its key (`EXC-261` is Exciter issue #261), its title, its Markdown body as a document, its labels and its milestone. Closed issues are done, with the date they closed.
- [ ] **Dependencies:** "Depends on" references become blocking links, also across projects (`Cloudster1/Exciter#59` in an Armature issue links to `EXC-59`).
- [ ] **People:** no GitHub login or email address is copied. Reporters and assignees are the seed's demo people.
- [ ] **Snapshot:** the content comes from a snapshot in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network. `make demo-snapshot` refreshes it with `gh` and records the date and commit of each repository.
- [ ] **Partners:** once Exciter and Stator add their part, the issues show their requirements and pages as remote links. Those tools push the links; Armature needs nothing new for that.

## Tests

- Go unit: the snapshot maps to issues (keys, states, closing dates, labels, milestones, people, "Depends on" links).
- Integration: add the demo; a second add and a taken key are refused; each project holds as many issues as its snapshot; a cross-project blocking link exists.
- Browser: add the demo from Settings, open `EXC-261` and see its blocking link, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- Beside `backend/internal/demo`, through `issue.ImportInput` with `KeyNum` for the GitHub number and `ExternalKey` set to the issue URL, so that a renewed snapshot updates the issues instead of copying them.
- One JSON file per repository; the keys join `demo.Keys` so the two demos never clash.
- A decision in `docs/decisions.md`: why a snapshot and not a live import from GitHub.

Depends on: nothing.

issues.title: Let people in by group mapping at sign-in and at token exchange
issues.body:
When an installation maps a Keycloak group to a role, a person in that group is already allowed in; they should not have to be invited or admitted from a join request first. Otherwise Stator and Exciter cannot connect a person to Armature at sign-in (the token exchange from #280 refuses anyone without standing), and people have to connect by themselves.

- At OIDC sign-in, a person without standing whose `groups` claim holds a group that has a role assignment is created and admitted with that role, then their groups are synced as today.
- The same at a token exchange from a partner app (`fromIdentityProvider` in `backend/internal/oauth/token.go`): a person who never opened Armature is connected by Stator or Exciter at their first sign-in there. The account is matched or created by verified email as at sign-in.
- A person in no mapped group still gets a join request, as today; a disabled person is refused.
- Off unless an administrator turns it on: `admitByGroup` on `PUT /api/v1/oidc-provider` (default false), so existing installations behave as before. The setting shows on the sign-in settings page with a sentence saying what it does.
- The audit log records each admission as admitted by group <name>.
- Tests: sign-in and exchange for a new person in a mapped group, in an unmapped group, and one disabled in Keycloak; with the setting off nothing changes.

**Here today:** `backend/internal/oidc/signin.go` refuses a person without standing (`ErrNotAMember`) and records a join request; `token.go` answers such a person `invalid_grant`.


Part of the connected deployment from [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo): the three tools share one Keycloak realm (`dynamo`), a person signs in to whichever tool they open, and the tools connect that person to each other without a click or a pasted token. Dynamo only tests the combination and ships an umbrella chart whose setup job wires the tools once through their admin APIs.

issues.title: Report token exchange as a capability
issues.body:
Armature accepts a token exchange (RFC 8693) for a partner app since #280, but does not say so in `GET /api/v1/meta`. Stator and Exciter must decide from capabilities, not versions, whether to exchange a person's Keycloak token at sign-in.

- Report `oauth.token-exchange@1` in `capabilities`, with its promise in `capabilities.go` and `docs/integration.md`: `POST /api/v1/oauth/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`, `subject_token` an access token of the installation's OIDC provider whose `azp` is the app's `keycloakClientId` and whose `aud` holds Armature's client, the app authenticating with its own credentials; the answer an access and a refresh token within the person's rights, never `webhooks.partner`.
- Name and promise are listed in Dynamo's `docs/compatibility.md`.
- A test holds the capability to the grant really being served.


Part of the connected deployment from [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo): the three tools share one Keycloak realm (`dynamo`), a person signs in to whichever tool they open, and the tools connect that person to each other without a click or a pasted token. Dynamo only tests the combination and ships an umbrella chart whose setup job wires the tools once through their admin APIs.

issues.title: The chart's roles Job fails: Kubernetes turns $$ in its SQL into $
issues.body:
Installing the chart with the bundled Postgres fails: the roles Job never finishes, so the install's post-install hooks fail and every api and worker crash-loops on `password authentication failed for user "armature_app"`.

```
ERROR:  syntax error at or near "$"
LINE 1: DO $
```

`templates/job-roles.yaml` runs its SQL from the container's `args`, where Kubernetes reads `$$` as an escaped `$`, so `DO $$ ... $$;` reaches Postgres as `DO $ ... $;`. Stator's chart ran into the same and uses a named tag (`DO $roles$ ... $roles$;`) with a comment saying why.

- Use a named dollar-quote tag in the roles Job, and anywhere else the chart puts `$$` into a command or args.
- A test that installs the chart (as Stator's and Exciter's chart-install tests do) would have caught it; at least the golden render should not contain `$$` inside args.

Found by Dynamo's kind test, which installs Stator, Armature and Exciter together (praetorianer777/Dynamo#10).

issues.title: Move personal pages to the avatar menu and settings to an area of their own, and add a narrow layout
issues.body:
The three tools that run together (Stator, Armature, Exciter) are moving to one menu layout, described in praetorianer777/Dynamo#12: personal pages under the avatar, administration in a settings area of its own, the sidebar for work. Armature keeps both in its sidebar today, where every agent sees all 13 Settings entries and most pages then refuse them. This is Armature's part.

## Avatar menu
The avatar at the bottom of the rail opens a menu, folded or not. Today it only links to the profile when the sidebar is open.
- A header with name, email and role.
- Your profile, Notification settings (the Notifications section of the profile), Watching, Themes, Access tokens (today's "API tokens"), Connected apps (`/settings/connected-apps`, now only on the hub and by URL), in this order.
- The connected tools (#327).
- **Settings**, for administrators only (`canAdministerOrg`), opening the settings area.
- Sign out.

## Settings area
The Settings group leaves the main sidebar. `/settings` and the pages under it get a sidebar of their own in place of the main one, headed by "Back to Armature", which returns to the last page outside it.
- **You:** the avatar menu's personal pages in its order, then Exciter account and Stator account.
- **Settings**, for administrators only (`canAdministerOrg`), in this order: Installation, Access, Users, Single sign-on (if it gets a page of its own), Holidays, Workflows, Labels, Automation, Fields, Issue view, Webhooks, Audit log.

The `/settings` hub:
- Add Issue view.
- The Everyone card becomes Settings and is shown to administrators only.
- The You card gets the "You" group's pages.

## Sidebar
- The Work & Plan group and the project group stay.
- **Saved searches** (`/filters`) joins the Work & Plan group, after Search.
- **Notifications:** rename the sidebar entry Inbox to Notifications, keep the route `/inbox`, and give it the unread badge the rail bell has.
- No personal and no installation-wide pages. **Foot:** the build stamp.

## Rail
- The bell opens a panel with the latest notifications, "Mark all read", "See all" (`/inbox`) and "Notification settings", like the other two tools. Today it only navigates.

## Palette
- The palette reaches every page of the sidebar, the avatar menu and the settings area, from the lists they read.
- Today its settings part is a fixed list that leaves out Installation, Automation, Webhooks, Fields, Issue view, Audit log, Connected apps and Profile.
- Its settings entries follow the same administrator rule as the settings area.

## Narrow screens
Armature is the one tool without a narrow layout.
- Below 768px, hide the rail and sidebar. A thin strip with an "Open the navigation" button opens a drawer with the same groups, and the avatar menu's entries, the theme switch and the build stamp in its foot. In the settings area the drawer holds the settings sidebar.
- Stator's and Exciter's `features/shell/Sidebar.tsx` and `state.ts` already do this, with `SIDEBAR_DRAWER_BELOW_PX = 768`.
- Read the width on resize, not only at mount.

## Done when
- The avatar menu holds personal pages, the connected tools, Settings for administrators and Sign out.
- A non-administrator sees no Settings entry or group, and the palette offers them no settings page.
- Every page the hub lists is reachable from the avatar menu or the settings area, and from the palette.
- At 375px wide the drawer opens, holds every group and closes on following a link.
- The e2e suite checks the avatar menu and the settings area for an administrator and a member, and the drawer at phone width.

issues.title: Use the suite's shared names for menu entries
issues.milestone: One look with Stator and Exciter

This issue is this tool's part. The renames go in the i18n strings, English and German, so page titles, breadcrumbs, links and the palette say the same as the menu. The menu layout itself is a separate issue: Cloudster1/Armature#308.

## Renames

issues.title: Run the tests on every pull request, as Stator, Exciter and Rotor do
issues.body:
Stator, Exciter and Rotor each run their tests on GitHub for every pull request, every push to main and every night. Armature runs only the Conventions check there, so a pull request can be merged with a failing test layer and nobody sees it until someone runs `make test-all` by hand.

Add workflows of the same kind:

- **CI**: the four layers (`make test`, `make npm ARGS="run test"` with the typecheck, `make test-integration`, `make test-e2e`) and the chart's lint and golden render, as jobs side by side, on every pull request, on main and nightly. A run by hand can repeat the gate to show a flaky test.
- **Chart install**: install `deploy/charts/armature` with `values-demo.yaml` into a throwaway kind cluster, check the hook Jobs, the workloads and a sign-in, then upgrade it with no failed health check. Runs when something the chart installs changes, as in Stator and Exciter.
- **Deps**: govulncheck and npm audit, nightly and on a pull request that changes a dependency, as in Rotor. Not a required check.

issues.title: Take golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 for four HTTP/2 advisories
issues.body:
`make audit-go` (govulncheck) finds four advisories in `golang.org/x/net` v0.58.0 that the backend can reach, all in the HTTP/2 server and fixed in v0.60.0:

- GO-2026-6617: HTTP/2 server crash due to an HPACK encoder race
- GO-2026-6612: double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams
- GO-2026-6611: excessive CPU from repeated initial window changes
- GO-2026-6603: HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers

Take v0.60.0 so the Deps workflow from #311 passes.

issues.title: The demo chart's seed Job fails when SeaweedFS is still starting
issues.body:
Installing the chart with `values-demo.yaml` sometimes fails at the post-install seed Job:

```
level=ERROR msg="seed failed" error="attachment bucket: check bucket armature-attachments: Head \"http://armature-seaweedfs-s3:8333/armature-attachments\": dial tcp 10.96.1.243:8333: connect: connection refused"
Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: failed post-install: 1 error occurred:
	* job armature-seed failed: BackoffLimitExceeded
```

The seed runs as soon as migrate has, and asks for the bucket once. On a fresh install SeaweedFS's master may still be electing a leader, so the S3 gateway refuses the connection. The Job's two tries come about ten seconds apart and both fail, and the install fails with them. The chart install test from #311 hit this on one of two runs.

The seed already gives Gitea a minute to start. It should give the object store the same wait.

issues.title: Two browser scenarios fail now and then on GitHub's runners
issues.body:
Since the CI workflow from #311 runs the browser suite on GitHub's runners, two scenarios fail now and then. They never failed in any local run.

- **an API token can be created and revoked**: failed in 3 of 5 runs (#312, twice on #316). It reads the page as soon as the path is `/settings/tokens` and expects "No tokens yet", but the list may still be loading, so the text holds only the sidebar:
  ```
  the list starts empty: "Collapse the sidebar\nHome\nSearch\n...\nSET" does not contain "No tokens yet"
  ```
- **a request is followed by somebody who was only named**: failed once (#312). It takes the first mail about the request that reaches the follower. On a slow runner, the request's receipt can go out after the follower was added, and reach them first:
  ```
  the mail says who did it: "We have your request HELZ81W0G-1: The lift is stuck ..." does not contain "added you"
  ```

The token scenario should wait for its empty list. The desk scenario should ask `mailFor` for the mail `saying: "added you"`, as other scenarios do when two mails about one issue may arrive in either order.

issues.title: Take Dynamo's realm with the token-exchange audience mappers
issues.body:
`realm-check` compares `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` with Dynamo's canonical realm on `main`. Dynamo is adding the audience mappers token exchange needs (praetorianer777/Dynamo#13, PR praetorianer777/Dynamo#15):
- `stator`: `armature`, `exciter`;
- `exciter`: `armature`, `stator`;
- `armature`: `exciter`.

Armature takes a partner's exchanged token only if its `aud` holds `armature`, so without the mapper on `stator` and `exciter`, Stator's and Exciter's sign-in exchanges at Armature are refused. Once Dynamo's PR is merged, this copy differs and `realm-check` fails, so both should land together. Stator pins this copy, so Stator follows from here.

## Done when
- `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` is Dynamo's realm byte for byte, and `realm-check` and the seed's realm test pass.

issues.title: Shard the browser suite in CI
issues.body:
In CI, the `e2e` job is the slowest: about 9 minutes in a single job on the last green `main`, so the whole run waits for it. Stator splits its browser suite into 4 jobs of 9 to 11 minutes, and Exciter into 2.

**Change:** shard the browser suite in CI with Playwright's `--shard=i/n`. Run a matrix of jobs, each with its own stack, and merge the blob reports into one HTML report (`merge-reports`). Keep the tests that need the installation to themselves, if there are any, in one shard or in a serial phase of their own, as Stator does with its instance phase.

## Done when
- CI's browser jobs each take at most about 4 to 5 minutes, and the merged report lists every test once.
- Running the suite locally without a shard is unchanged.

issues.title: Create the Go cache directories before a container mounts them
issues.body:
`make release VERSION=0.1.0` in a fresh clone failed inside its own test:

```
failed to initialize build cache at /gocache: mkdir /gocache/00: permission denied
```

**Cause:** the Go targets mount `.cache/gocache` and `.cache/gomod` into a container that runs as the caller (`-u $(UID):$(GID)`). In a fresh clone those directories don't exist yet, so Docker creates them for the mount, owned by root. The container can't write to them, and the caller can't remove them either.

**Fix:** make the cache directories an order-only prerequisite of every target that mounts them, created by `mkdir -p` as the caller, as Dynamo does with `$(GO_CACHE)`.

## Done when
- `make test` and `make release DRY_RUN=1 VERSION=x.y.z` work in a fresh clone, and `.cache` is owned by the caller afterwards.

issues.title: Bootstrap the first administrator and members from the chart, as Stator and Exciter do
issues.body:
Armature has no bootstrap. A new installation is owned by whoever signs up first (`auth.signup: first`). Stator and Exciter instead run a bootstrap Job: it creates the organization, its first local administrator from a Secret, and the members to let in before their first sign-in.

**Why it matters:**
- **Takeover window.** In a cluster, Armature's ingress is public once its pods are ready, and nothing has signed up yet. Whoever reaches it first owns the installation. In Dynamo's umbrella chart, `dynamo-connect` signs up first, but only after all three tools' hooks. That's minutes of an open installation on a public address.
- **Workaround in Dynamo.** Dynamo's chart carries `armatureAdmin` and makes the owner itself, while the other two take theirs from their own charts (praetorianer777/Dynamo#20).

**Change:** a bootstrap as in Stator's and Exciter's charts:
- `bootstrap.admin.email`, with the password from a Secret the chart makes when none is named (`<fullname>-bootstrap-admin`, keys `username` and `password`, random when blank, kept across upgrades);
- `bootstrap.members`: emails and roles let in before their first sign-in;
- a post-install/post-upgrade Job that applies them idempotently, before the app answers sign-ups;
- with a bootstrap, `signup` defaults to `closed`, so there's no first-come owner. `first` stays for a setup without the bootstrap.

## Done when
- `helm install` with `bootstrap.admin.email` set leaves an installation owned by that account, with no open first sign-up at any point, and the chart test checks it.
- Rerunning the Job on an upgrade changes nothing, and a password changed in its Secret is kept.

issues.title: Sign in silently when the identity provider already has a session
issues.body:
Someone signed in to Armature, Stator or Exciter through the suite's Keycloak realm, who then opens another of the three, lands on its sign-in page and has to click "Sign in". Keycloak still has their session, so the click sends them there and straight back, signed in, without a password. The click is all that's left, but it happens on every first visit and on every link from one tool to another. This was seen on a real Dynamo install, where Keycloak returns at once.

**Change:** on a visit without a session, Armature first tries a silent sign-in:
- **The request:** a top-level redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with `prompt=none`, the usual `state`, PKCE and `nonce`, and the page the person asked for.
- **Keycloak still has a session:** the callback signs the person in, as a normal sign-in does, with the same group mapping and membership checks, and returns them to that page.
- **No session** (`error=login_required`, `interaction_required` or `consent_required`): the callback shows the sign-in page as today, and remembers for the browser session (a short-lived cookie) that the silent try already failed, so there's no redirect loop and no second round trip on the next page.
- **Only when single sign-on is configured:** with local accounts only, nothing changes.
- **Not after signing out:** a sign-out sets the same marker, so the person isn't signed straight back in. With RP-initiated logout at the provider, the provider's session ends too.
- **Can be turned off:** a setting, for example `auth.silentSignIn` in the chart, on by default when an OIDC provider is set.

## Done when
- In the integration or browser tests, with a provider that has a session, opening a deep link without a session lands on that page signed in, with no click. Without a provider session, it lands on the sign-in page, and the next page doesn't redirect again.
- After signing out, the next visit shows the sign-in page.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `auth.silent-sign-in@1`, so the suite's tests can rely on it (praetorianer777/Dynamo#2).

issues.title: Link the connected tools in the avatar menu
issues.body:
Clicking one's profile picture opens a small menu. When Armature is connected to Stator or Exciter, that menu should also link to them, so people can switch tools in one click.

## What the menu shows
- Under the account entries, a group "Switch to" with one entry per tool Armature is connected to: its name and its icon.
- Each entry opens that tool's home at the public address of the connection an administrator set up, the one dynamo-connect configures.
- It is a plain link, so the browser's open-in-new-tab works too.
- A tool is listed once the organization's connection to it is configured, whether or not the person connected their own account there; with single sign-on the other tool signs them in.
- A tool that is not connected, or whose connection an administrator removed, is not listed. With none, the group is not shown.
- Everyone signed in sees it, guests included, since the other tool decides what they may see.

## Fits the shared layout
The menus of the three tools are moving to one layout (praetorianer777/Dynamo#12). The group belongs in the avatar menu wherever that layout keeps it, in the same place and under the same name in all three. The same issue is filed in each tool.

## Done when
- With Stator and Exciter connected, the avatar menu lists both and each link opens that tool's home.
- With one connected, only it is listed; with none, the group is gone.
- A test covers each of these.

issues.title: Take an issue's description as Markdown

Stator (PUT /pages/{id}/markdown) and Exciter (statementMarkdown) take Markdown; Armature takes an issue's description only as its own document. Anything that brings issues in from elsewhere, such as Dynamo's sample import of GitHub issues, therefore shows `### Describe the bug`, lists and code as plain text, or has to write its own converter to Armature's document.

issues.title: Offer a project's repositories, an issue's development and pull requests over MCP
issues.body:
## User story

As a partner tool such as Rotor, we want to read a project's repositories and an issue's development, make a branch for an issue and open its pull request over MCP, as the person, so a workflow can implement an issue in the repository Armature already connects.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Reading:** MCP tools `list_repositories {projectKey}` and `get_issue_development {issueKey}` over the existing `GET /projects/{key}/repositories` and `GET /issues/{key}/development`, both read-only.
- **A branch:** `create_issue_branch {issueKey, repository, name?, from?}` over `POST /issues/{key}/branches`, needing `issue.write` on the issue.
- **A pull request:** a new `POST /issues/{key}/pull-requests` and its tool `open_pull_request {issueKey, repository, branch, title, body, draft?}` on GitHub, GitLab and Gitea:
  - written with the repository's token, only for a person who may edit the issue;
  - refused for the default branch and for a branch not made for an issue;
  - recorded on the issue as the pull requests the host reports are.
- **Errors:** a repository without a token answers with `ErrNoToken`'s sentence.
- `docs/integration.md` lists the tools.

## Tests

- **Unit:** each host's pull request request against recorded responses.
- **Integration:** the tools through `POST /mcp` with a partner token; a reader is refused.

## Implementation

- `backend/internal/git` (`pull_requests.go`, `branches.go`, and per host `github.go`, `gitlab.go`, `gitea.go`).
- Entries in `backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go`, so `mcp_tools.go` offers them.

## Depends on

- #305. Cloudster1/Rotor#137 waits on it.

issues.title: Let a connected app clone and push an issue branch through Armature, as the person
issues.body:
## User story

As a partner tool such as Rotor, we want to clone a project's repository and push to an issue's branch through Armature with the person's token, so a workflow writes code with that person's rights and the host's token never leaves Armature.

## Acceptance criteria

- **The proxy:** git smart HTTP at `/api/v1/git/{projectKey}/{repo}.git` (`info/refs`, `git-upload-pack`, `git-receive-pack`), forwarded to the host with the repository's token.
- **Who:** a partner bearer token. A clone needs `read` and the right to browse the project; a push needs a new scope `git.write` and the right to edit the issue whose branch is pushed.
- **Where to:** pushes go only to branches Armature made for an issue (`create_issue_branch`, Cloudster1/Armature#332). The default branch, tags, deletions and force pushes are refused with a sentence the git client prints.
- **Limits:** a size cap per push and a rate limit per token.
- **Audit:** every push is in the audit log with the person and the app.
- The OAuth metadata and `docs/oauth.md` list `git.write`.

## Tests

- **Integration:** against a Gitea container: a clone, a push to an issue branch, a push to the default branch refused, a push without `git.write` refused, a reader refused.

## Implementation

- `backend/internal/git`; read the receive-pack commands to check every ref before forwarding.

## Depends on

- #332. Cloudster1/Rotor#137 waits on it.

issues.title: Propose the moves that start each blocked issue after the issues blocking it
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead with a plan full of dependencies, I want Armature to tell me which issues start before the work blocking them is done, and where they would have to go, so that I can line the plan up in one step instead of dragging bar after bar.

This is the first part of the Auto plan milestone: the engine and a proposal that changes nothing. Applying it is #346, the button in the timeline #347.

## What happens today

- A plan is a reading of the project's issues and owns no tables (`backend/internal/plan/service.go:387`, `ForProjectMatching`).
- Blocks links are the only dependencies (`issue.LinkTypeBlocks`, `issue.Blocker{BlockerKey, BlockedKey}` and `Blockers(ctx, projectKey)` in `backend/internal/issue/links.go:28,32,261`). A blocker may be in another project.
- `plan.Check` (`backend/internal/plan/plan.go:157`) already warns `blocked-too-early` when `!blocked.Start.After(*blocker.Due)` (:200), so a blocked issue may start the day after its blocker's due date at the earliest. Starting on the same day counts as too early (`TestCheckTreatsSameDayAsTooEarly`).
- Cycles cannot exist: the service refuses them (`refuseBlockCycle`) and so does the trigger in `00024_link_cycles.sql`.
- Working days per team, with holidays and working weeks, are in `plan.Workdays` (`backend/internal/plan/workdays.go`).
- Nothing in the backend sorts issues by their dependencies. The only topological order is the frontend graph layout (`web/src/features/plan/graph.ts`, `layers`).

## The rule

Push only. An issue moves only when it starts on or before the due date of one of its blockers. It then starts on the first working day after the latest blocker's due date and keeps its length in working days, counted on its team's calendar (the project's when it has no team). Moving it can make the issues it blocks too early in turn, so the pass runs in dependency order and carries the moves along. Slack is kept: nothing is pulled earlier.

These stay where they are and only constrain the others:
- issues in a done status (`Issue.IsDone`);
- issues already under way (status not in the to-do category and start before today), which keep their start;
- blockers in another project;
- issues the plan's query does not match, when the plan is filtered;
- parents whose span is derived from their children (`Item.Derived`).

An issue with only one date, or none, is neither moved nor used as a constraint here. Placing those is its own issue in this milestone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pure function in `backend/internal/plan/align.go`, such as `Align(items []Item, blockers []issue.Blocker, days Workdays, today time.Time) Alignment`, returns the moves (key, current start and due, new start and due) in dependency order.
- [ ] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/plan/align` with an optional `q` (the plan's NQL) returns that proposal and the warnings the plan would have after it: moved past a milestone, outside its parent, and any `blocked-too-early` it could not resolve because the blocker is fixed. It writes nothing.
- [ ] It needs `IssueWrite` on the project; someone who may only browse is refused with a sentence that says so.
- [ ] A move never lands on a weekend or a holiday of the issue's team, and an issue of five working days is five working days after it moves.
- [ ] `make openapi` regenerates `api/openapi.json` and `web/src/api/schema.d.ts`.

## Tests

- **Go unit (`align_test.go`):** a chain A blocks B blocks C, a diamond, a blocker with a later due than the other blocker, a move across a weekend and a holiday, each fixed case above, and an already aligned plan that proposes nothing.
- **Integration (`backend/test/plan_test.go`):** the proposal over HTTP for a project made with `h.newProject`, a cross-project blocker that is not moved, a browse-only person refused, nothing written. Add the operation to `endpoints_test.go`.

issues.title: Apply a plan's moves in one transaction, refused when an issue moved since the preview
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead who has reviewed an auto plan (#345), I want every proposed move saved at once, so that the plan is never left half aligned and nobody else's change is overwritten without me seeing it.

## What happens today

- Dates are saved one issue at a time by `PUT /issues/{issueKey}/schedule` (`backend/internal/httpapi/plan_handlers.go:55`), through `issue.Service.Schedule` (`backend/internal/issue/schedule.go:20`). It locks the row, runs `CheckDates`, writes both ends, records `startDate` and `dueDate` in the history and emits `issue.updated`.
- Bulk edit (`backend/internal/bulk/bulk.go`) cannot change dates and runs one transaction per issue, so it can stop half way by design.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/plan/schedule` takes a list of `{key, expected: {startDate, dueDate}, startDate, dueDate}`, at most a named number of entries (a constant beside `bulk.MaxSelection`).
- [ ] It locks every row in one transaction, and refuses the whole list when any issue's dates are no longer the `expected` ones, naming the issue: "PROJ-12 was moved since the preview; preview the auto plan again." Nothing is saved in that case.
- [ ] Every issue must be in the project and writable by the person (`IssueWrite`); one that is not refuses the list with a sentence naming it.
- [ ] Each issue gets its history entries and its own `issue.updated`, as a single schedule change does. Webhooks, automation and watcher notifications therefore see one change per moved issue, as today; the endpoint documents that.
- [ ] The single-issue schedule and this endpoint share one update, factored out of `issue.Service.Schedule`, so both keep the same checks.
- [ ] `make openapi` regenerates the document and `schema.d.ts`.

## Tests

- **Go unit:** the limit and the request validation.
- **Integration:** all of three moves saved, a stale `expected` refuses all three and leaves the dates as they were, a key from another project refused, the history of each moved issue, one `issue.updated` per issue in the outbox. Prove the guard below the service too: a backwards range written straight through SQL is refused by `issue_range_not_backwards`.

issues.title: Auto plan the timeline from its toolbar, with a preview of every move
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead looking at the timeline, I want an Auto plan button that shows me what would move before anything does, so that I can align the plan with its dependencies and still decide.

## What happens today

- The toolbar is `web/src/features/plan/PlanToolbar.tsx:15`, the timeline `web/src/features/plan/Timeline.tsx`. Dependency arrows are drawn by `DependencyArrows` (:1021), and a `blocked-too-early` warning marks a dependency scheduled too early.
- Every date change is made by hand, bar by bar, through `useSchedule()` (`web/src/api/plan.ts:129`).
- The timeline draws drag handles for everyone and lets the server refuse. `canWriteIssues` (`web/src/api/access.ts`) is already used elsewhere, for example `routes/calendar.tsx`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An "Auto plan" button in the toolbar of the management and sprints views, shown to people who can write issues in the project.
- [ ] It asks for the proposal of #345 with the plan's current query and opens a preview: each moved bar drawn as a ghost at its new place over the current one, and a list of the moves ("PROJ-4 moves from 3 Nov to 10 Nov, 5 working days") with the warnings that would remain.
- [ ] **Apply** saves the moves through `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/plan/schedule` with the expected dates from the proposal, closes the preview and refreshes the plan. **Cancel** closes it and changes nothing.
- [ ] When nothing needs to move it says "Every issue already starts after the issues blocking it." and offers nothing to apply.
- [ ] A refusal (someone moved an issue meanwhile) shows its sentence in the preview and offers to preview again.
- [ ] Dragging is off while the preview is open, and Escape closes it.
- [ ] Copy and limits live in `web/src/config.ts`.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the preview list and ghosts from a proposal, the empty case, the refusal, the button hidden without write access.
- **e2e (`e2e/scenarios/plan.mjs`):** `createProject`, two issues scheduled with `scheduleIssue`, a dependency drawn with `dragLink` so the blocked one starts too early, Auto plan, Apply; `barRange` shows the blocked bar after its blocker and the warning is gone. A second case cancels and finds the dates unchanged.

issues.title: Undo an auto plan in one step
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead who applied an auto plan and did not like the result, I want to undo it in one step, so that trying it costs nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After Apply, the toast says how many issues moved and offers Undo (`useToast`'s `action`, `web/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx:13`).
- [ ] Undo sends the reverse moves through `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/plan/schedule`, expecting the dates the auto plan set, so the issues return to where they were.
- [ ] If any of them was changed since, the undo saves nothing and says which one: "PROJ-4 was changed after the auto plan, so it was not undone. Move it back by hand or run auto plan again."
- [ ] The history of each issue shows the move and the move back.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the toast and its Undo, the refusal sentence.
- **e2e (`e2e/scenarios/plan.mjs`):** auto plan, Undo, `barRange` shows the original dates.

issues.title: Place issues without dates from their estimate when auto planning
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead with estimated work that has no dates yet, I want auto plan to place it after what blocks it, so that a new plan gets a first shape without dragging every bar.

## What happens today

- The timeline header counts "N not on the plan yet" (`web/src/features/plan/Timeline.tsx:480`) and the resources page lists that work (`web/src/features/resources/UnplacedWork.tsx`), but nothing places it.
- `plan/resources.go` already turns remaining or estimated time into hours (`hoursOf`, :309) and spreads hours over a team's working days (`spreadHours`, :322).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The auto plan preview has an option "Also place issues without dates", off by default.
- [ ] With it, an issue that has neither date but has remaining time or a time estimate is placed: it starts on the first working day after its latest blocker, or today when nothing blocks it, and lasts as many of its team's working days as its hours need at the team's daily time.
- [ ] Placed issues show in the preview as new ghost bars, marked as placed, not moved, and are saved with the rest on Apply (with an expected empty start and due).
- [ ] An issue without any estimate is not placed and is listed as "Not placed: it has no estimate."
- [ ] Issues placed this way then constrain the issues they block, in the same pass.

## Tests

- **Go unit:** a placed issue after its blocker, one placed from today, the length from hours over a calendar with a holiday, one without an estimate left out.
- **Integration:** the proposal with the option, and Apply saving a placed issue.
- **Vitest:** the option and the placed ghosts.
- **e2e:** an estimated issue without dates, blocked by a scheduled one, gets a bar after it.

issues.title: A dependency on a parent holds back its children
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead who links epics, I want a dependency on an epic to hold back the work inside it, so that "the API epic blocks the client epic" means the client's stories start after the API's are done.

## What happens today

- `plan.Check` (`backend/internal/plan/plan.go:157`) and the auto plan only compare the two linked issues. A parent with derived dates (`Item.Derived`, rolled up by `Rollup` at :118) is not moved, and its children ignore the link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Blocks link from or to a parent counts for every descendant with dates: each descendant of the blocked issue must start after the latest due date among the blocker and its descendants.
- [ ] `Check`'s `blocked-too-early` warning and the auto plan use the same rule, so after an auto plan no such warning is left that it could have resolved.
- [ ] The warning names the link it comes from, so a lead sees that the story is too early because of its epic.

## Tests

- **Go unit (`plan_test.go`, `align_test.go`):** an epic blocking an epic, an issue blocking an epic, an epic blocking an issue, nested two levels.
- **Integration:** the proposal for a tree made with `h.buildTree`.
- **e2e:** two epics with a story each and a link between the epics; auto plan moves the second story after the first.

issues.title: Offer to move the issues it blocks when a blocker is dragged later
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who just dragged an issue later on the timeline, I want to be offered to move the work it blocks along with it, so that the plan stays aligned without opening the auto plan each time.

## What happens today

- A drag in `web/src/features/plan/Timeline.tsx` (released at :350-366) saves only that issue. The issues it blocks keep their dates and get a `blocked-too-early` warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a drag that leaves issues it blocks, directly or further down, starting too early, a toast offers "Move the 3 issues it blocks".
- [ ] Taking it runs the auto plan rule only on that issue's downstream issues and saves through `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/plan/schedule`, with the same refusal when something changed meanwhile, and Undo as after an auto plan.
- [ ] A drag that leaves no dependent too early, or moves an issue earlier, shows nothing extra.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the offer appears only when a dependent starts too early, and counts the downstream issues.
- **e2e (`e2e/scenarios/plan.mjs`):** `dragBar` a blocker past its dependent, take the offer, `barRange` shows the dependent after it.

issues.title: Offer auto plan to agents over MCP
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working with an agent connected over MCP, I want it to see what auto plan would move and apply it when I agree, so that "line up the plan" works from the agent too.

## What happens today

- `GET /projects/{projectKey}/plan` is offered as the tool `get_plan` (`backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go:333`). Scheduling has no tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The proposal endpoint is offered as `align_plan` and the apply endpoint as `apply_plan_schedule`, each with a `toolHelp` that says the first changes nothing and the second needs the expected dates from it.
- [ ] Both act as the person, with the same permission checks and refusals as over HTTP.

## Tests

issues.title: Give the shell the skip link, states and panel ids Stator and Exciter have
issues.milestone: One look with Stator and Exciter
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter give their shell a few landmarks and states that Armature's lacks, and two of Armature's controls point at elements that are not there. This issue is part of the milestone "One look with Stator and Exciter".

## What happens today

issues.title: Speak English and German from one catalogue, as Stator and Exciter do
issues.milestone: One look with Stator and Exciter
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter speak English and German from one catalogue. Armature has no catalogue: every string is written into the component, and the profile's Language select changes only how dates and numbers are formatted. #309 asks for the suite's shared names "in the i18n strings, English and German", which needs this first. This issue is part of the milestone "One look with Stator and Exciter".

## What happens today

- There is no `web/src/i18n`. Copy is hard-coded in English across `web/src`.
- The profile's Language select (`web/src/routes/profile.tsx:139`) offers "Same as the browser (...)" and says it changes formatting only while the interface is English.

## Asked

- [ ] A `web/src/i18n` in the shape Stator and Exciter use, with English and German, and the language taken from the profile's choice or the browser.

No test asks for a 403: every refusal on the 11 operations is 404 or 422. The `automation_rule` checks and the feature trigger are never tried through SQL. In the browser, work.mjs has 2 scenarios. They create a rule on `/projects/$key/automation`, open its run log and read an incoming address. No scenario opens `/settings/automation`, and "Run now", "Turn off", "Delete", "Add a condition" and the schedule fields are clicked by no scenario. No vitest file renders RulesPanel.tsx or RuleEditor.tsx; only describe.test.ts exists. coverage-summary.json lists both at 100%, but on 1 line each, so they were never loaded.

## Gaps

Go integration:

The rule keeps its name and `enabled`, and no `automation_run` row is written.

A second rule with the same name in the project, by `POST` and by `PATCH`: 422 "A rule with that name is already here."
- [ ] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/automation/rules` on a project with automation turned off: 409 `feature_off`. Also decide and assert what happens to a project's existing rules once automation is turned off. Today `Handle` still runs them (see report).
- [ ] The actions no test runs, through `Handle` with the run log read back: `assign` to reporter, actor, none and a person's id; `create_subissue` (the subtask's parent is the issue); `set_field` summary and due `+3`; a `transition` the workflow offers (the issue moves); and `send_mail` to assignee, watchers and an address. Each gets its note in `actions`, and an unknown address fails the run with a sentence.
- [ ] Conditions `field_equals` (priority, assignee `none`, label) and `actor_role`: a miss is a skipped run whose reason names the field or the role ("the actor is member, not admin"). An `actor_role` condition must also hold back "Run now" and an incoming call with no issue. Today it is not asked (see report).
- [ ] Triggers: `issue.updated` with `field: "assignee"` skips "assignee did not change" on a priority edit. `comment.added` runs on a person's comment. `sla.breached` runs on a desk request whose clock runs out. `allowOwnEvents: true` runs on the automation account's own comment.
