An edit that keeps `incoming` keeps the address. `GET .../runs?limit=1` returns one run, and after `DELETE` the runs are gone and `GET .../runs` is 404.
- [ ] `POST /automation/hooks/{token}`: a body that is not JSON is 400 "The body has to be JSON.", one over 256 KB is 400, and an empty body is 202. Handling the queued `automation.incoming` event creates the issue, or comments on the posted `issueKey`. A project rule given an `issueKey` from another project fails its run "is not in". The API test stops at the 202 today.
- [ ] Rules for all projects: one runs on an issue in any project. Its `create_issue` action fails the run with "a rule across all projects has no project to create in".
- [ ] MCP: `list_automation_rules` and `run_automation_rule` through `tools/call` return the rules and the run. A token scoped `read` gets an error from `run_automation_rule`, and no run is written. Neither tool is called in mcp_test.go.

issues.title: Test ranking, quick filters and board permissions on the board
issues.body:
Boards have broad cover. board_test.go and board_lanes_test.go drive the board service through moves, reordering, swimlane merging, unmapped states, new workflow statuses and finished work. A reader is shown refused six configuration calls with 403 and the rows left alone. e2e/scenarios/board.mjs has 15 scenarios covering dragging between lanes, a forbidden drag, merging and reordering lanes, a team board's lanes, renaming, retyping and deleting a board, and Only mine with the text filter. The gaps are in the details. Most refusals are asserted on the service only, not as HTTP status and code. `GET /boards/{boardID}/backlog` is only ever answered 200 in endpoints_walk_test.go. No scenario drops a card before another card: `dragCardTo` always drops on the lane. The Assignee, Label, Type and Epic chips, the row grouping drawn on the board, the card limit and "Add swimlane" are never used in the browser. No vitest test renders `BoardView`: routes/board.test.tsx mocks it, so the 100% in coverage-summary.json is one counted statement.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/board/move` as a Reader: 403, and the issue's status and rank are unchanged. Without `issueKey` or `swimlaneId`: 400. Into a lane with no transition behind it: 422 `validation_failed`, with a message naming the current status. Into In Review with no assignee: 422, naming the validator's field. All of these are asserted on `ws.boards.Move` today, never over HTTP.
- [ ] Ranking over HTTP: `board/move` with `afterKey`/`beforeKey` in the same lane gives the order `GET /projects/{projectKey}/board` returns afterwards, with no `transition` in the answer. A move into another lane whose `afterKey`/`beforeKey` are out of rank order is refused with a 422 sentence, and the issue keeps its status.
- [ ] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/boards` by a User and by a Scrum master: 403, and no board is added. A second board named like an existing one in another case: 409. A blank name: 422. `type: "agile"`: 400 "A board is either scrum or kanban."
- [ ] `DELETE /boards/{boardID}` of the project's only board: 409 "a project keeps at least one board", and the board stays. `DELETE /boards/{boardID}` and `PATCH /boards/{boardID}` with `name` or `type` as a Reader: 403. The reader list in board_lanes_test.go covers only lanes, `groupBy` and `doneForDays`.
- [ ] Swimlane refusals over HTTP, with code and the lane rows unchanged: `PUT /boards/{boardID}/swimlanes` naming only some lanes, `DELETE` of the last lane, `PATCH .../swimlanes/{id}` with a status another lane holds, `wipLimit: -1`, and a blank name. Today these are tried through the service only, or not at all.
- [ ] `GET /boards/{boardID}/backlog`: a team board's backlog holds that team's unfinished, uncommitted work in rank order. It leaves out work committed to a sprint, done work and another team's work, and follows a rank change made with `board/move`. Add `/api/v1/boards/{far}/backlog` to the 404 list in project_boundaries_test.go.
- [ ] MCP `list_boards` and `get_board` through `/mcp` for a project member, and refused for a person outside the project. Only `create_issue`, `get_issue` and `search_issues` are called through `/mcp` today.

Database guards:
- [ ] Through SQL: `board_swimlane.wip_limit = -1`, a blank `board_swimlane.name`, a blank `board.name`, and a second board in the same project named the same apart from case (`board_project_name_idx`). Each must be refused. Only `done_for_days` and the second mapping of a status are tried today.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] Rank within a lane: drag the third To Do card onto the first card, so it drops before it. The lane reads third, first, second, keeps that order after a reload, and no "Moved through the workflow" status shows. Dropping a card back on itself leaves the order as it was. No scenario fires a dragover on a `[data-card]` today; add a `dragCardBefore` helper.
- [ ] Quick filter chips: open "Assignee", "Label", "Type" and "Epic" (`data-quick-filter="label"` and the others), then pick a value (`data-quick-filter-value`). The cards narrow, AND across chips and OR within one, the address carries `label=` and `type=`, and a reload keeps them. Today only "Only mine" and the text box are used.
- [ ] Rows within lanes: on "Configure swimlanes", press "Priority", then "Issue type", then "Assignee". After "Done configuring" each lane shows its cards under row headings (High, Medium; Bug, Task; a person's name). Today a scenario only checks that the chip is pressed.
- [ ] Card limit: set "Card limit" 1 on In Progress, then drag two cards in. Neither drag is refused, and the lane count reads "2 / 1" and is marked over the limit. No scenario puts a lane over its limit today.
- [ ] "Add swimlane": submit "New swimlane name" Blocked with no states, and the lane says "No states: nothing can be here". Untick In Review in its own lane, tick it in Blocked, and a card in review shows in Blocked. Also cover "Cancel" on the form, and "Move Blocked right" (only "left" is clicked today).
- [ ] A drag a validator refuses: unassign a card in In Progress, then drag it to In Review. The alert names the missing assignee, and the card stays in In Progress. Only the no-transition refusal is tried today.
- [ ] Who sees what. A User sees no "Configure swimlanes", "New board", "Rename", "Change type" or "Delete", but can still drag a card. A Reader's drag is refused and the card stays put. A Project administrator gets "Configure swimlanes" and "New board", and their changes save.
- [ ] "New board" with "Draws from" set to a team (`#board-team`): the new board shows only that team's cards. "Give X a board" is covered in sprints.mjs, but no scenario picks the team in the form.
- [ ] "Change type" a kanban board to scrum while no sprint runs. The board says "No sprint is running", and "Go to sprints" lands on `/projects/$key/sprints`. No scenario clicks "Go to sprints" today.

Component (vitest):
- [ ] `BoardView` drop: the `afterKey`/`beforeKey` sent for a drop at the top, between two cards, at the end, and beside a card the filter hides. A drop on itself sends no request. The move toast and the "Moved through the workflow" line come from the server's answer, and a refusal shows `ErrorBanner`. The `DRAG_MIME` payload is read off the event when the ref is empty.
- [ ] `BoardView` drawing: the lane count and title over the limit, filtered ("2 of 3") and limited ("3 / 5"). The "No states" line, the unmapped banner listing keys, and the scrum empty state with no sprint. Also `groupCards` (rows sorted by name, `none` one row) and `describeEnd` (today, tomorrow, in n days, yesterday, n days ago); neither has a test, and api/boards.ts is at 14% lines.
- [ ] routes/board.tsx: "New board" and "Configure swimlanes" are drawn for a person who holds `board.configure` on the project, and not for one who does not, whatever their role across all projects. Today the only case is a mocked owner.


## Done when
- Every control on `/projects/$key/board` (chips, drag before a card, lane editor, board picker, New board) is used by a scenario that asserts what the board shows afterwards, including for a person without the permission.
- Every board, swimlane and move refusal has an integration test asserting status, code and unchanged rows. The backlog endpoint is asserted for its content and its project wall.
- `BoardView` is rendered by a vitest test that covers the drop arithmetic and the lane counts.

issues.title: Test sprint planning, its refusals and the sprint board end to end
issues.body:
The sprint lifecycle is well tested at the service: sprint_test.go (12 tests), sprint_stream_test.go, sprint_snapshot_test.go, sprint_reads_test.go and team_delete_test.go cover starting one at a time, carrying work on, the frozen report, deletion returning work, teams' streams and the daily snapshots, and they try the one-active index, the dates of a running sprint, reopening and the cross-project sprint straight through SQL. Over HTTP the sprint operations are only walked through once in endpoints_test.go; the only refusals there are creating a sprint by role (enforcement_test.go) and the far project's sprint (project_boundaries_test.go, any 4xx). Every 409 and 422 the service gives is asserted on the Go error, never on the status and code a client gets. In the browser, sprints.mjs (10 scenarios) commits work only through `#issue-sprint` on the issue page: no scenario uses the move select on a sprint page row, deletes a sprint, sees a start or date refusal, or opens the board of a planned or finished sprint by its state. SprintPlanning.tsx has 54% branch coverage and its three vitest cases do not reach capacity, carry or the closed card.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `PATCH /sprints/{sprintID}`, `POST /sprints/{sprintID}/start`, `POST /sprints/{sprintID}/complete` and `DELETE /sprints/{sprintID}` by a person with the User role in the project (issue.write, no sprint.manage): 403 forbidden each, and the sprint's name, state and dates are unchanged. Today only `POST /projects/{projectKey}/sprints` is tried by role.
- [ ] `PUT /issues/{issueKey}/sprint` by a User: 403, the issue stays in the backlog. `PUT /issues/{issueKey}/estimate` by a Reader: 403, the estimate is unchanged.
- [ ] 422 validation_failed with a sentence, and no row made or changed: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/sprints` with a blank name, with `endsOn` before `startsOn`, with `capacity: -1`; the same three on `PATCH /sprints/{sprintID}`; `PUT /issues/{issueKey}/estimate` with `-1`.
- [ ] 409 conflict with the message a person reads: start a second sprint ("Sprint 1 is already running"), start one with no dates, complete one twice, `PATCH` a closed sprint, `PUT /issues/{issueKey}/sprint` into a closed sprint. `DELETE` of a running and of a closed sprint ("has already run") is not tried at any layer; its issues must stay in it.
- [ ] `POST /sprints/{sprintID}/complete` with `moveTo` set to the sprint itself: 422, and the sprint is still running. With `moveTo` a closed sprint: 409; with another project's sprint: 404. Nothing moves in any of them.
- [ ] `GET /sprints/{sprintID}/board` over HTTP for a closed sprint shows the work finished in it, and for an unknown id is 404 not_found. sprint_board_test.go tries the service only, and only planned sprints.

Database guards:
- [ ] Through SQL: `sprint_name_not_blank` (name `'  '`), `sprint_range_not_backwards` (ends before it starts), `sprint_capacity_not_negative`, and `UPDATE sprint SET state = 'future'` on a running sprint ("a running sprint cannot go back to being planned"). None is tried today.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] Sprints page row select "Move <KEY> to" (`#move-<KEY>`): move an issue from the Backlog into Sprint 1, then back. It appears under the sprint card, the Backlog heading count goes down and up again. No scenario uses `#move-` today.
- [ ] "Delete" on an empty planned sprint card: cancel in the confirm keeps it, confirm removes the card. No scenario clicks it; sprints.mjs only checks it is absent on a card with work.
- [ ] "Complete sprint" with "Carry the rest to the backlog": the unfinished issue shows under Backlog, the card says "Completed" with its completed count, and offers no "Start sprint", no "Delete", no carry select and no move select on its rows.
- [ ] "Start sprint" on a card without dates shows the refusal on the card ("needs a start and an end"), and setting the "to" date before "From" shows the date refusal under the card's settings. No scenario reaches either.
- [ ] Sprint board `/projects/$key/sprints/$sprintId/board` for a planned and for a completed sprint: the header tag (`data-sprint-state`) reads "Planned" and "Over", the "Sprints" crumb goes back, and a quick filter keeps the sprint's address. plan-calendar.mjs opens a planned sprint's board but checks neither.
- [ ] Estimate on the issue page (`#issue-estimate`): clearing it shows "unsized" on the sprints page row and drops the points from the capacity; `0` shows "0 pts" and is counted as sized.
- [ ] A person with the User role opens `/projects/$key/sprints` and an issue: no "Add sprint", "Start sprint", "Complete sprint" or move select, and `#issue-sprint` cannot be changed.
- [ ] Velocity widget on the dashboard after two completed sprints shows each sprint's committed and completed points. dashboards.mjs only removes the widget and checks its "not narrowed" note.

Component (vitest):
- [ ] SprintPlanning: the capacity input sends `capacity: null` when emptied, nothing when unchanged or not a number; "Complete sprint" sends `moveTo: null` by default and the picked sprint's id otherwise; the carry options leave out the sprint itself and closed sprints; a closed card renders no settings and no move select.
- [ ] EstimateField and SprintField: an emptied estimate sends `estimate: null`, `0` sends 0, an unchanged one sends nothing; a refusal shows its message; SprintField keeps showing the closed sprint an issue is already in.

## Done when
- Every sprint operation has an integration test asserting 403 for a person without "Plan sprints" and its 409 or 422 with code and unchanged rows.
- The sprint table's check constraints and state guard are each tried straight through SQL.
- Every control on the sprints page, the sprint board and the issue's sprint and estimate fields is reached by a browser scenario that asserts its effect.

issues.body:

issues.title: Test roles, groups, users and the audit log with their refusals
issues.body:
Access is well covered where it counts most: `TestWhatEachRoleMayDo` walks the five roles, `roles_test.go` refuses bad roles with 409 and 422, `users_test.go` and `second_factor_test.go` refuse bad accounts and rules, and `triggers_without_organization_test.go` tries the role, group, last administrator and built-in role guards straight through SQL. Eighteen browser scenarios in `access.mjs`, `users.mjs` and `installation.mjs` cover granting, the role matrix's tick, making, resetting and switching off a user, and renaming the installation; RoleTable, RoleMatrix, MemberList, InvitePanel, ProviderSettings and JoinRequests have vitest suites. What is missing is the administrator's refusals to everybody else: no test asks a non-administrator to change roles, groups, single sign-on or the audit log and expects 403 (`TestWhatEachRoleMayDo` counts any non-2xx). The group operations are never refused at all (`endpoints_walk_test.go` only succeeds). In the browser nobody adds a person to a group, takes them out of it or deletes the group. On Users, nobody renames a user, changes their role, turns off their two-step sign-in or reactivates them, and nobody lets in or declines somebody waiting to be let in. On the Matrix nobody renames or deletes a role, and on the audit log nobody filters by date or turns a page.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] Groups refused: a project administrator's `POST /groups`, `DELETE /groups/{groupID}`, `POST /groups/{groupID}/members` and `DELETE /groups/{groupID}/members/{userID}` are 403 and the group's rows are unchanged. The same name twice is refused with its code. Adding a stranger is 422 (`ErrNotAMember`). Adding to or removing from a group whose `source` is `oidc` is refused (`ErrManagedElsewhere`) and its members stay.
- [ ] Roles refused to a non-administrator: `POST /roles`, `PATCH /roles/{roleKey}` and `DELETE /roles/{roleKey}` by a project administrator are 403. The role list is unchanged and a holder of the role keeps what it grants.
- [ ] `DELETE /role-assignments/{assignmentID}`: revoking the last `global_administrator` grant over the API is 422 `validation_failed` and the grant stays (only `perm.Store.Revoke` is tried, in rbac_test.go). A project administrator revoking another person's grant is 403, and an unknown id is 404.
- [ ] `PUT /oidc-provider`: a member is 403. An issuer that is not an `https` URL, or no client id, is 422 naming the field. In both cases `GET /oidc-provider` still returns the saved provider.
- [ ] `GET /audit` and `GET /audit/export` as a member are 403. `from` and `to` keep only the rows inside the dates, and `before` returns the next page with no row repeated (only bad values are tried today, in org_level_test.go).
- [ ] Users refused to a member: `PATCH /users/{userID}`, `PUT /users/{userID}/password` and `DELETE /members/{userID}` are 403. `PATCH /users/{userID}` with role `wizard` is 422, and the account is unchanged.
- [ ] MCP: `list_audit_log` and `list_members` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what the HTTP calls answer. A member's token gets `isError` from `list_audit_log`, with the permission named. No test calls either tool today.

Database guards:
- [ ] Two sessions revoke the last two `global_administrator` grants at the same moment: one of them must be refused. Then the same `DELETE FROM role_assignment` through SQL. No trigger guards it today, so this needs a guard as well as a test (see the separate report).
- [ ] Through SQL, a `role_assignment` for a user whose standing is `customer`, and a `group_member` row for one. Decide whether the database refuses them, as `team_member_guard` already refuses a customer, and try it either way. Today both guards accept any standing that is not NULL.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] Groups tab: grant "User" over a project to a new group, then add bob with "Add somebody to <group>" and "Add". Bob then opens the project. "Remove" beside bob takes it away again, and "Delete" on the group, after the confirm, removes the card. No scenario clicks Add, Remove or Delete on a group today. The existing scenario only checks the Roles table.
- [ ] A group made with a "Provider claim" shows "from the identity provider" and offers no "Add" or "Remove".
- [ ] Matrix: "Actions for <role>" then "Rename or describe" (`data-action="rename-role"`) renames the column and the Roles tab's option. "Delete" (`delete-role`) asks, removes the column, and the person who held the role loses what it granted. "Delete" is disabled for a built-in role. No scenario opens `role-menu` today.
- [ ] Matrix: untick `sprint.manage` for a role somebody holds. On their next page load "New sprint" is gone and the API refuses them.
- [ ] Roles tab: "Only this role" narrows the grants to one role, and "Grant pages" turns to the second page with the address keeping it.
- [ ] Users: from "Actions for <name>", "Rename" shows the new name in the user's own sidebar. "Change role" to Administrator gives them the Settings card and `/settings/users`, and back to Member takes both away. "Turn off two-step sign-in" lets them sign in with the password alone. "Reactivate" lets a switched off person sign in again. Only "Deactivate" and "Set password" are clicked today.
- [ ] Users: somebody the provider vouched for waits under "Waiting to be let in". "Let in as member" (`admit-request`) makes them a member who signs in, and "Turn away" (`decline-request`) removes the row. Today a scenario only checks that the empty list takes no room.
- [ ] Audit log: "From" and "To" narrow the rows to the dates chosen. "Older" (`audit-older`) and "Newer" walk the pages. "Export CSV" after narrowing to `role.granted` downloads a file whose rows are all `role.granted`. Today only the action filter is used, and only the export button's presence is checked.

Component (vitest):
- [ ] GroupList: a provider group offers no picker and no Remove. Delete asks first and names what is lost. Add is disabled until somebody is picked. No test file exists today.
- [ ] UserTable: each item in "Actions for <name>" is disabled on the administrator's own row, "Change role" on an owner, "Set password" on a provider account, "Turn off two-step sign-in" without a second factor and "Working week" on a customer. No test file exists today.

## Done when
- Every control on `/settings/access` (all five tabs), `/settings/users` and `/settings/audit` is reached by a browser scenario that checks its effect on another person.
- Every access, users and audit operation has an integration test for a 403 by a non-administrator and a 422 with its code for bad input, and checks that the rows are unchanged.
- The last global administrator is kept by the database as well as the service, and the test proves it through SQL.

issues.title: Test creating, setting up and archiving projects with their refusals
issues.body:
Projects are covered along their main path. `endpoints_test.go` walks every project operation once. `projects_page_test.go` pages and searches the list, and `project_restore_test.go` refuses a reader's archive and restore with 403. `project_features_test.go`, `project_docs_test.go`, `resources_test.go` and `template_test.go` refuse bad features, documentation links, groupings and templates with 409 or 422. In the browser, `projects.mjs` creates a project through the form, finds and pages the list, archives and restores from the row and from settings, and saves a documentation link. `templates.mjs` turns a feature on. The gaps are in what a project is made with and what its administrator changes. No test sends a key that is taken or badly shaped to `POST /projects` or `GET /projects/key-check`. No test sets a project's lead or kind anywhere (`grep '"leadId"' backend/test` finds nothing). No test changes an archived project's settings over the API. Only `sprint_feature_on` of the eight feature triggers is tried through SQL. In the browser nobody renames a project, picks its lead, turns a feature off or switches its planning method. The create form's key refusals and "Cancel" are never clicked, and nobody checks what a member who does not administer sees.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `POST /projects`: a key that another project holds is 409 (`ErrKeyTaken`, "already in use"), even when that project is archived. A key that is lower case, one character long, eleven long or starts with a digit is 422 naming `key`. An empty name is 422 naming `name`. No project row is written in any of these cases.
- [ ] `GET /projects/key-check`: a taken key answers `available: false`, a badly shaped one `valid: false`, and `?name=` suggests a key that is free. Today it is called once, for a suggestion, and the answer is not read.
- [ ] `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}` `leadId`: a member becomes the lead, the list and `GET /projects/{projectKey}` name them, and `null` clears the lead. A customer, a stranger or an unknown id is 422 and the lead is unchanged.
- [ ] `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}`: an empty name is 422 and the old name stays. A rename is seen by another member's `GET /projects`. `kind` service to software on a desk that has a mail request type is refused, and the desk keeps its type.
- [ ] An archived project: `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}` (name, features, planning method) is refused with the archived error and the row is unchanged. `POST /projects/{projectKey}/restore` on a project that is not archived is 404 "project not found" today (`Restore` in internal/project/service.go:599 matches only archived rows). Decide on a code that says it is not archived, and assert it.
- [ ] `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `POST .../restore` by a User or Scrum master over the project are 403, with the permission named. `TestWhatEachRoleMayDo` only counts PATCH as not 2xx, and the archive refusal is tried only for a reader.
- [ ] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/status-updates` by a reader is 403 and the history is unchanged. A `targetOn` that is not a date is 422.
- [ ] MCP: `list_projects`, `get_project`, `list_status_updates` and `post_status_update` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what the HTTP calls answer, and a read-only token gets `isError` from `post_status_update`. No test calls them today.

Database guards:
- [ ] With a feature off, through SQL, an `INSERT` into milestone, version, component, team, git_repository, automation_rule and import_job is refused with "this project does not use ...". Only sprint is tried today (project_features_test.go).
- [ ] `project_key_shape`, `project_name_not_blank`, `project_docs_url_shape` and `project_docs_label_shape`: try each through SQL (a lower case key, a blank name, `ftp://` docs, a label without an address) and watch it refuse.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] "New project" form: typing a key another project holds shows "That key is already in use." and disables "Create project". `1AB` shows "Use 2 to 10 letters or digits, starting with a letter.". "Cancel" closes the form and creates nothing. No scenario reaches either error today.
- [ ] Project settings: change "Project name" and "Description", then "Save changes". "Project settings saved" appears, and the new name shows in the sidebar and on another member's `/projects` row. No scenario renames a project today.
- [ ] Project settings "Lead": pick a member and save. The projects list's Lead column names them, and "Nobody in particular" clears it.
- [ ] Features: turn "Sprints" off (`data-feature="sprints"`) on a scrum project that has a sprint. The sidebar drops Sprints, `/projects/$key/sprints` shows the `data-feature-off` notice, and turning it back on shows the old sprint again. Today a scenario only turns a feature on.
- [ ] "Planning method" (`data-planning-method`): switch a kanban project to scrum. Resources goes back to "Planned by team", and the person grouping is disabled. No scenario clicks the method today.
- [ ] A member granted only User over the project: the row on `/projects` has no "Actions for <name>" menu, `/projects` has no "New project", and `/projects/$key/settings` says "Only the project's administrators change its settings".

A feature switch sends the whole list with the feature added or removed. The field errors from a 422 land under their fields. Today only archive and restore are tested.

issues.title: Test setting up the service desk and its portal end to end
issues.body:
The desk's journeys are covered well. About 30 integration files cover it: `desk_test.go`, `desk_extras_test.go`, `desk_companies_test.go`, `desk_clocks_test.go`, `desk_sla_follow_test.go`, `desk_holidays_test.go`, `open_door_test.go`, `trusted_domains_test.go`, `portal_code_test.go`, `takeover_test.go`, `mail_raise_test.go`, `inbound_test.go`, `watchers_test.go` and more. They raise, follow, reply to, reopen and rate requests, read mail in over POP3 and send mail out through TLS and relays. Companies, the open door and sessions are tried straight through SQL. `mailin` (87%) and `mail` (90%) have strong unit tests. Fourteen browser scenarios in `desk.mjs`, `desk-mail.mjs`, `desk-companies.mjs` and `holidays.mjs` walk a customer from the door to a rating. The gaps sit on the administrator's side of `/projects/$key/service-desk`. Making a request type, an article, a canned response, a company and the door is driven in the browser. Editing or deleting any of them is not, and neither are the SLA goals or the weekly hours (`grep -rn "data-request-type-edit\|data-policy\|Save goals" e2e/` finds nothing). In `/projects/$key/queues` only "All" is ever clicked. On the API, configuring the desk is never refused to an agent or a customer, except for companies and the holiday calendar. In vitest, `features/desk` is at 36% of lines, with `DeskExtras.tsx` at 31% and `SlaBadge.tsx` at 10%.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] Request types refused: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/request-types`, `PATCH /request-types/{requestTypeID}` and `DELETE /request-types/{requestTypeID}` by an agent with only User over the desk are 403. An empty name, an issue type that does not exist and another project's team are 422 naming the field. The portal's list of types is unchanged.
- [ ] `PATCH /sla-policies/{policyID}`: an agent with User is 403. A negative or zero goal is 422. The running clocks keep their goal in both cases.
- [ ] Articles and canned responses: `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/articles/{articleID}` and `/canned-responses/{responseID}` by a customer and by a User agent are 403, and the rows are unchanged. `PATCH /articles/{articleID}` with an empty title is 422. A customer's `GET /portal/articles/{articleID}` for a draft is 404.
- [ ] `POST /csat/{token}` with a score of 0 or 7 is 422 and the request stays unrated. Only `desk.Service.Rate` is tried today (desk_extras_test.go:102).
- [ ] Portal input: `POST /portal/requests` with an empty summary is 422. `POST /portal/requests/{issueKey}/replies` with no words is 422, and from a customer who is not on the request and not in its company is 404. The comment list is unchanged in each case.
- [ ] Deleting the request type the desk's mail raises (`mailRequestTypeId`): the project's type goes to null, and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/mail-address` says new mail raises nothing. The next new mail is answered as unmatched instead of raising a request.
- [ ] MCP: `list_articles` through `/api/v1/mcp` lists the desk's articles to an agent's token and none of the drafts to a customer's. No test calls it today.

Database guards:
- [ ] Through SQL: `csat_rating_score_range` with a score of 6, `request_type_name_not_blank`, `kb_article_title_not_blank`, `canned_response_body_not_blank` and `sla_timer.goal_minutes = 0`. Each must be refused. None is tried today.
- [ ] `UPDATE project SET kind = 'software'` on a desk whose `mail_request_type_id` is set is refused by `project_mail_request_type_check`, since the trigger also watches `kind`. Moving an existing `user_session` to a desk whose door asks for a code (`UPDATE ... SET portal_project_id`) is refused by `user_session_open_door`. Only the inserts are tried today.

Go unit:
- [ ] `desk.summaryOf`: an empty or whitespace subject becomes "Request by mail", and a subject over `issue.MaxSummary` is cut on a rune. `isDaemon` covers `postmaster`, `noreply` and `no-reply-...`. `bareAddress` covers `"Ada <ada@x.test>"`, a bare address and a missing `>`.

Browser (e2e scenario):

Editing it changes what the portal reads, and deleting it after the confirm removes it. Editing and deleting a canned response changes or removes its `data-canned-option` in an issue's "canned-responses" menu.

issues.title: Test connecting repositories, the git proxy and their refusals end to end
issues.body:
The flow in from the hosts is well tested: git_test.go and its neighbours (git_checks, git_merge_once, git_smart_once, git_branch_deleted, gitea) cover pushes, pull requests, CI and smart commands for GitHub, GitLab and Gitea; git_proxy_test.go clones and pushes through `/git/{projectKey}/{owner}/{name}` with real git and refuses the default branch, a foreign branch, force pushes, tags, deletions, readers and missing `git.write`; git_mcp_test.go drives all four git tools with their main refusals; and two scenarios in e2e/scenarios/git.mjs connect a repository, take a signed delivery and make branches on Gitea. The gaps are the edges: nobody tries a repository change as a project member without administer (only another project's administrator, who gets 404), none of the connect, pull request or proxy refusal sentences in errors.go and git_proxy.go appear in any test, `PATCH` and `DELETE /repositories/{id}` are only answered 200 and 204 in endpoints_walk_test.go without checking their effect, and on the Repositories page no scenario clicks "Rotate secret", "Disconnect", "Save token" or "Remove token". RepositoryList.tsx has no vitest test at all.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] A member of the project without administer (`perm.User`): `POST /projects/{key}/repositories`, `PATCH /repositories/{id}`, `POST /repositories/{id}/rotate-secret` and `DELETE /repositories/{id}` each answer 403, and the repository keeps its secret, token and settings. Today only TestARepositoryIsBehindItsProjectsWall tries, as another project's administrator (404).
- [ ] `POST /projects/{key}/repositories` in a project with the repositories feature off: 409 `feature_off` with the "does not use repositories" sentence and no row. project_features_test.go tries only sprints.
- [ ] Connect refusals over HTTP: a name without owner/name, host `bitbucket` ("The host must be github, gitlab or gitea."), the same repository twice and `ACME/Portal` after `acme/portal` (409, `git.ErrNameTaken`), and `PATCH` with an empty `defaultBranch`. No test names `ErrBadHost` or `ErrNameTaken` for git.
- [ ] `PATCH /repositories/{id}` effects: a replaced `accessToken` is the one the next `POST /issues/{key}/branches` sends to the host; `accessToken: ""` turns `hasToken` false and the next branch is 409 `no_token`; a new `transitionOnMerge` moves the issue on the next merge.
- [ ] `DELETE /repositories/{id}`: its webhook address answers 404 afterwards, and the issue's `GET /issues/{key}/development` no longer lists its commits and branches (the rows cascade).
- [ ] `POST /repositories/{id}/rotate-secret`: a delivery signed with the old secret is 401 `webhook_unauthenticated` afterwards, one with the new secret is 200. Today the test only checks the new secret differs.
- [ ] `POST /git/webhooks/{id}` over HTTP for GitLab with a wrong `X-Gitlab-Token` (401) and for a `ping` and an unknown event (200, nothing recorded); these are only unit tested in internal/git/hosts_test.go.
- [ ] `POST /issues/{key}/pull-requests` over HTTP: no title (400, `ErrNoTitle`), a second one from the same branch (409), a name two hosts carry (409, `ErrAmbiguousName`) and a host that refuses (502 `host_refused`); no test reaches `ErrNoTitle` or `ErrAmbiguousName`.
- [ ] Git proxy refusals with their sentences: a customer's token (403 "Customers use the portal."), a revoked token (401 "not valid any more"), a session without a token (401 "Clone and push with a token"), an app without `read` (403), a repository with no access token (409), owner/name on two hosts (409 "Two hosts carry"), and `info/refs` without `?service=` (400 "smart protocol only"). None of these strings is in a test.
- [ ] Git proxy when the host fails: the host refuses Armature's token (502 "The host refused Armature's token"), answers 404 (502), or cannot be reached (502), each as a git error line.
- [ ] `git push --signed` is answered with "Armature does not forward signed pushes", and a push larger than `git.MaxPushBytes` is refused whole; both write an `audit_log` row `git.push` with outcome `refused` and the host is never called. Only the `forwarded` row is asserted today.

Database guards:
- [ ] `INSERT INTO git_repository` for a project whose `features` lack `repositories` is refused by `git_repository_feature_on` ("this project does not use repositories") straight through SQL.
- [ ] The unique index on `git_repository (project_id, host, lower(name))`: a second row differing only in case is refused through SQL, while the same name on another host is accepted.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] Repositories page: "Rotate secret" shows the handout again with a new `webhook-secret`, and a delivery signed with the old one is refused. No scenario clicks it today.
- [ ] "Disconnect" removes the card and brings back "No repositories connected", and the issue's Development section is gone. No scenario clicks it today.
- [ ] "Add an access token" then "Save token" turns the card's "read only" into "read and write" and "Create branch" can choose the repository; "Remove token" turns it back. No scenario clicks either.
- [ ] Connect form: pick a transition in "When a pull request is merged, take"; the card says "merging takes <name>" and merging a pull request on Gitea moves the issue. "Cancel" closes the form without a repository, and connecting the same repository twice shows the conflict in the form's error banner.
- [ ] Development panel: the "CI passed" or "CI failed" button opens `ci-checks` with each check; with only a read only repository "Create branch" shows `no-token` and "Create" is disabled; "Cancel" closes the form without a request.

No test imports RepositoryList.tsx today (its 100% in coverage-summary.json is the one line of an unloaded file).

issues.title: Call every MCP tool in a test and refuse each one it should
issues.body:
Of the 56 MCP tools (the `tool:` fields in openapi_operations.go), only seven are ever called through `POST /mcp` in a test: `create_issue`, `get_issue` and `search_issues` (mcp_test.go, assistant_test.go) and `list_repositories`, `get_issue_development`, `create_issue_branch` and `open_pull_request` (git_mcp_test.go). The other 49 are only checked for their shape by the unit tests in internal/httpapi/mcp_test.go. Four of the seven are never refused at all (`get_issue`, `search_issues`, `list_repositories`, `get_issue_development`), and `create_issue` is refused only for a read-only key, never for a missing permission. The OAuth server is otherwise well covered by oauth_test.go: metadata, PKCE, code reuse, refresh rotation and revocation all have tests. What is missing is the second way of authenticating (`client_secret_post`), public apps past registration, one app holding another's code or token, and the brakes on `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/revoke` and `/oauth/register`.

Never called through /mcp (49). Reads: `get_board`, `get_hierarchy`, `get_holiday_calendar`, `get_plan`, `get_project`, `get_report`, `get_resources`, `get_sprint_board`, `get_working_week`, `list_absences`, `list_allocations`, `list_articles`, `list_audit_log`, `list_automation_rules`, `list_boards`, `list_comments`, `list_components`, `list_dashboards`, `list_filters`, `list_holiday_calendars`, `list_issue_types`, `list_labels`, `list_members`, `list_milestones`, `list_notifications`, `list_project_issues`, `list_projects`, `list_project_statuses`, `list_remote_links`, `list_sprints`, `list_statuses`, `list_status_updates`, `list_teams`, `list_transitions`, `list_versions`, `run_filter`, `whoami`. Writes: `add_comment`, `add_remote_link`, `bulk_edit_issues`, `post_status_update`, `record_absence`, `remove_remote_link`, `run_automation_rule`, `set_allocation`, `set_holidays`, `set_working_week`, `transition_issue`, `update_issue`.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] One table test calls each of the 37 read tools above through `/mcp` as a member with a token, with arguments from one prepared project, and asserts `structuredContent` equals the body of the HTTP call it stands for.
- [ ] The same table as a person outside the project (or with another project's ids): every project-scoped read answers `isError` with the not found sentence, never data. This also refuses `get_issue`, `search_issues`, `list_repositories` and `get_issue_development` for the first time.

- [ ] Issue writes through `/mcp`: `update_issue`, `transition_issue`, `add_comment` and `bulk_edit_issues` each land and read back; each is refused for a `perm.Reader` (`isError` naming the permission, issue unchanged) and for a read-only key ("only read"). Add `create_issue` by a Reader to the same table.
- [ ] `add_remote_link`, `list_remote_links` and `remove_remote_link` through `/mcp` as a partner app with `issue.write`: the page is added, listed and removed; with `read` only, adding is refused "allowed to read only".

- [ ] `post_status_update` and `run_automation_rule` through `/mcp` land for a project administrator and are refused for a member without the permission, with nothing posted or run.
- [ ] Planning writes through `/mcp`: `set_working_week` lands for an administrator and is refused to a member (it is administrators only); `set_allocation` lands for a project administrator and is refused to a member; `record_absence` for a person outside the caller's teams is refused with nothing recorded.

issues.title: Test webhooks from the settings page to the receiver, and every event topic
issues.body:
The pieces are tested one at a time. The outbox and relay are covered in outbox_test.go and outbox_slow_group_test.go, the consumer's retries, stops, kills and dead letters in consumer_test.go, signing, backoff and redelivery through the service in TestAWebhookIsSignedRetriedAndRedelivered (automation_test.go), envelope versions in webhook_version_test.go, a hanging endpoint in webhook_concurrency_test.go and send_test.go, and the audit trail of endpoint changes in audit_admin_test.go. What is missing is the whole path: no test runs `webhook.NewConsumer`, `RunSender`, `automation.NewConsumer` or `RunSchedules`, the loops cmd/worker/main.go starts, so nothing shows an event reaching a receiver through the stream. Also missing: a member's 403 on any `/webhooks` route, the last of the `MaxAttempts` retries, and the payload's `token` being stripped. Ten of the 23 topics in internal/events/events.go are never asserted to be published. In the browser only the partner scenario in connected-apps.mjs opens `/settings/webhooks`. No scenario adds a webhook, opens its deliveries, sends a test, rotates, deletes or redelivers, and routes/webhooks.tsx has no vitest test.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] A member calling `GET`, `POST /webhooks`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /webhooks/{id}`, `/rotate-secret`, `/test`, `/deliveries` and `/redeliver`: each 403 with the endpoint, its secret and its log unchanged. No test refuses a member on these routes.
- [ ] The worker's path end to end: an issue created over HTTP is relayed, picked up by the `webhooks` group through `webhook.NewConsumer(...).Run`, and posted by `RunSender` to a receiver as a signed `issue.created`. Today `Handle` and `SendDue` are called by hand.
- [ ] The last retry: after `MaxAttempts` failed attempts the delivery has no `nextAttemptAt`, nothing more is scheduled, and the log shows it failed; a redelivery by hand still goes.
- [ ] An endpoint that is turned off (`enabled: false`) is sent nothing for an event, and turning it on does not send what it missed. A removed endpoint's waiting retries are never posted.
- [ ] Rotating with `POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`: the next delivery verifies with the new secret and not the old one.
- [ ] `withoutSecrets`: an event whose payload carries `token` reaches the receiver without it. No test names the function or checks the field.

issues.title: Test the commands, migrations, readiness and chart beyond the happy path
issues.body:
The installation's own features are covered well. demo_project_test.go and suite_demo_test.go add the demos with their refusals, installation.mjs drives renaming and both demos in the browser, routes/installation.test.tsx covers the page, meta_test.go and api_test.go cover `/meta`, `/build` and `/readyz`, pdf_test.go and dashboards.mjs cover the render service, assistant_test.go covers the assistant against a fake provider, and deploy/kind/chart-install-test.sh installs, seeds twice, upgrades without a failed request and bootstraps. The gaps are where things go wrong. The commands in backend/cmd are at 0 to 3% unit coverage (assistant, installation and render are at 0%), and none of their refusals is tried. No test runs a migration's Down section. `/readyz` is never seen answering 503. A suite demo that failed cannot be retried. The ten `fail` and `required` messages in the chart's templates are never rendered in a test. The ServiceMonitor, TLS and existing Secret variants are in no golden file, and the kind install never touches the bucket, the render service or the worker's work.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] `/readyz` answers 503 `{"status":"unavailable"}` when the primary cannot be pinged (an api pointed at a closed database), and `/healthz` still answers 200. Every test today sees 200.

Following the message (remove ARM, EXC and STA, then `POST /installation/suite-demo` again) is answered 409 today, because nothing removes the `suite_demo` row. Fix that, then test the retry.
- [ ] A suite demo left `running` by a worker that died is picked up again, or reported, rather than staying `running` for good; `SuiteBuilder.Once` claims only `queued` rows.

- [ ] The assistant from the browser's side: a proposal confirmed through `POST /mcp` as a reader whose role cannot write is refused with nothing filed; a provider that times out answers 502 with the sentence.

Go unit:
- [ ] cmd/api: `trustedProxies` refuses an entry that is neither address nor CIDR with the `ARMATURE_TRUSTED_PROXIES` sentence, `splitList` drops blanks, and `asker` and `renderer` give the unavailable ones when nothing is configured.
- [ ] cmd/migrate: `up-to` without a version, an unknown command, and `migrate attachments` without both `ARMATURE_ATTACHMENT_DIR` and `ARMATURE_S3_ENDPOINT` each fail with their sentence.
- [ ] cmd/seed: it refuses `env=production` ("refusing to seed a production environment") and an installation another owner set up. cmd/worker: `ARMATURE_POP3_ADDR` without `ARMATURE_MAIL_INBOX` stops it with its sentence. Pull the checks out of `run()` where needed.

Today it checks only `/meta`, sign-in and the seed.

issues.title: Keep every route, menu entry, MCP tool and refusal covered, with coverage floors
issues.body:
Two guards hold today: `everyOperationWasExercised` in `backend/test/main_test.go` fails the integration run when one of the 390 operations was never answered or never refused, and `httpapi/openapi_test.go` keeps the router equal to the table. But `contract.uncovered` (`backend/test/contract_test.go`) counts any 4xx as a refusal, so an operation refused only with 401 or 404 passes; a static read of `backend/test` finds a 403 or 422 asserted next to a call for only about 100 of the 390 operations. Nothing ties the 69 web routes, the entries of `web/src/features/shell/places.ts` or the controls to the 193 browser scenarios: `e2e/scenarios/menus.mjs` reads the settings sidebar's labels but opens only "Audit log", and `/settings/automation` and `/settings/issue-view` are opened by no scenario. Nothing checks that every one of the 56 MCP tools is called through `POST /mcp`. Neither layer reports coverage: Go unit coverage is 21.8% of statements (0% in `cmd/*`, `internal/bulk`, `internal/sprint`, `internal/component`, `internal/installation`, `internal/render`), vitest reports 77.1% of lines (`features/desk` 36%, `src/api` 41%, `features/plan` 52%), and neither number is printed in CI. The vitest figure is too high: 123 of the 345 files it counts have one line or less, so they count as 100% though no test loads them. The workflow library cards, the automation files and `BoardView` are among them. The area issues of this milestone fill the gaps; this one keeps them filled.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [ ] Record the status codes per operation in `contract.observe` and fail the run for every operation that takes a session or a token and was never refused with 403 or 422 (or 409 where the table declares it). The few that have nothing to forbid and take no input are listed by name with why, as `unrefusable` does now.
- [ ] Fail the run for every MCP tool in the table that no test called through `POST /mcp` with `tools/call`, and for every tool never refused for a missing scope.
- [ ] The refusals list the error code too: a 422 must carry the code the handler declares, not only the status.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [ ] The runner records every path a scenario landed on (from `goto` and the router's navigations) and fails the full run when a route of `web/src/routes/index.ts` was never reached; a filtered run (`ONLY=`) skips the check, as `runFiltered` does for the Go suite.
- [ ] Every entry of `workPlaces`, `personalPlaces` and `settingsPlaces` is opened at least once by clicking it in the sidebar, the avatar menu or the settings area, not only by `goto`.
- [ ] A list of controls (test ids and `data-action` values from `docs/design/07-e2e-contract.md`) the runner checks were pressed, so a new button without a scenario shows up in the report.

Go unit and Component (vitest):
- [ ] `make test` writes a Go cover profile and `go tool cover -func` total; CI prints it and fails when it falls below a floor kept in the repository.
- [ ] Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` to the web devDependencies, run `vitest run --coverage` in CI with thresholds on lines and branches in `vite.config.ts`, starting at today's numbers.
- [ ] A test refuses lowering a floor: the floors only rise, raised by the pull request that adds the tests.

## Done when
- A full integration run fails for any operation without a specific 403 or 422 and for any MCP tool not called.
- A full browser run fails for any route or place never reached.
- Go and web coverage are reported in CI with floors that only rise.

issues.title: Take Dynamo's tightened Keycloak redirect URIs
issues.body:
The Conventions workflow's realm check now fails on every pull request: Dynamo, whose `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` is the canonical copy, changed the redirect URIs of its three confidential clients.

## What changed upstream
- `http://localhost*` became `http://localhost:*` and `http://localhost/*`.
- `http://127.0.0.1*` became `http://127.0.0.1:*` and `http://127.0.0.1/*`.

The old patterns let any host that starts with "localhost", such as `http://localhost.example.org`, receive a code. The new ones need a port or a path after the name.

## Asked
- [ ] `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` is Dynamo's copy again, and `make realm-check` passes.
- [ ] Single sign-on still works against the local stack: the integration and browser suites pass.

issues.title: The data-export scenario exports before the comment it checks for is saved
issues.body:
"A person can take their data and go, and their comment stays" (`e2e/scenarios/projects.mjs`) failed three times in CI on 2026-10-25 (#425, #433 and a local run): the exported file lacked the comment the scenario had just written.

## Why
The scenario types the comment into `#new-comment`, presses Comment, and then waits until the page's text includes the comment. `#new-comment` is the rich editor, a contenteditable element, so its own text satisfies that wait as soon as it is typed, before the comment is saved. The export then races the POST. The export itself reads from the primary (`ReadAdmin`), so it is not a replica lag.

## Asked
- [ ] The scenario waits for the saved comment in the activity list (`[data-comment]`) before it exports.

issues.title: TestRepositoriesOverTheAPI sometimes reads the issue before a commit's transition shows
issues.body:
## Problem

`TestRepositoriesOverTheAPI` failed once in CI on a pull request that changed only `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` (#399, run 40178429342):

```
git_test.go:777: status over the api = To Do, want In Progress
```

The test posts a signed push whose message carries `#start-progress`, sees the commit on the issue's development panel, and then reads the issue straight away. The status had not moved yet. The stack in that run has a read replica, so the read may have gone to a replica that had not caught up yet, or the transition may run after the webhook answers. Either way, the test assumes it sees the move at once.

## Done when

- It is clear whether the transition is written before the webhook answers, and whether the issue read can be served by a lagging replica.
- If the move is meant to be immediate, the read sees it every time. Otherwise the test waits for the move within a bound, as the other asynchronous checks do.
- The test passes in repeated runs (`-count` 20 or more).

```

```

issues.title: The Admin page holds everything an administrator sets
issues.body:
Administrative options live in the side view today. An administrator who opens `/settings/*` gets the work sidebar swapped for a settings sidebar (`settingsPlaces` in `web/src/features/shell/places.ts`, `SettingsGroups` in `Sidebar.tsx`), and personal and installation-wide entries share the one `/settings` hub. Nothing on the client stops a member from opening an admin URL; each page only hides its controls.

This gathers everything an installation administrator sets on one Admin page at `/admin`, visible only to them, and leaves `/settings` to the person's own pages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A layout route `/admin` under the app route, with an index that shows the sections as grouped cards and an in-page navigation (a list on the left at wide widths, a menu on narrow ones). Sections: People and access, Work, Integrations, Records.
- [ ] `settingsPlaces` becomes `adminPlaces`, each entry with its section, and drives the index, the navigation and the command palette.
- [ ] Installation, access, users, holidays, workflows (statuses, schemes, new, design), labels, automation, fields, issue view, connected apps, webhooks and audit move from `/settings/<x>` to `/admin/<x>`.
- [ ] Every old `/settings/<x>...` address of a moved page redirects to its `/admin` address with search and hash kept, replacing the history entry. `/settings/organization` lands on `/admin/installation`.
- [ ] `/admin` waits for the person's access in `beforeLoad`. Somebody who is not an administrator sees "Only administrators can open this page" and no admin request is sent.
- [ ] The work sidebar stays on `/admin`. Administrators get one "Admin" entry in it, and the account menu's "Settings" for administrators becomes "Admin".
- [ ] Links from project pages into the workflow library point at `/admin/workflows` and show only to installation administrators.
- [ ] `/settings` and its sidebar keep only the person's own pages (profile, notifications, watching, themes, tokens).
- [ ] Strings in English and German.

## Tests

Vitest:
- `places`, `Sidebar.test.tsx`, `AccountMenu.test.tsx` and `routes/settings.test.tsx` follow the new lists.
- A new `routes/admin.test.tsx`: a member is refused and no child page fetches anything, and the redirect table maps every old address.

Browser (e2e):
- A new `scenarios/admin.mjs`: an administrator reaches every section from the index, a member sees the refusal and no Admin entry, and `/settings/access?tab=members` lands on `/admin/access?tab=members`.
- `menus.mjs` checks the new lists, and every scenario that opened an admin `/settings/...` address uses the `/admin` one.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: A project's setup lives in its settings
issues.body:
A project's administrators set it up from a "project admin" group in the project sidebar (`projectSetupPages` in `Sidebar.tsx`): teams, workflows, fields, issue view, components, repositories, automation and import. The project's own Settings page holds only the general form. With the installation's settings moving to the Admin page, a project's setup should likewise leave the side view and live in the project's Settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `routes/project-settings.tsx` becomes a layout with tabs and an outlet, as `routes/workflows.tsx` is. The "only the project's administrators" check is made once, in the layout.
- [ ] Tabs: General, Teams, Workflows, Fields, Issue view, Components, Repositories, Automation and Import, each shown only when the project uses that feature.
- [ ] The old project addresses of these pages redirect to their tabs, keeping search and hash.
- [ ] The project-admin group leaves the sidebar. A project's administrators get one "Settings" entry among its pages; others do not see it.
- [ ] Strings in English and German.

## Tests

Vitest: `project-settings.test.tsx` shows only the tabs of features in use and refuses a member who does not administer. `Sidebar.test.tsx` has no project-admin group and one Settings entry for administrators.

Browser (e2e): `menus.mjs` follows the new sidebar. The teams, workflows, fields and components scenarios reach their pages through the Settings tabs. A reader of the project sees no Settings entry, and an old address lands on its tab.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: Administrators keep a library of issue types
issues.body:
Issue types are one global table (`issue_type`, migration 00002) seeded at bootstrap, and the API only lists them (`handleListIssueTypes` in `httpapi/meta_handlers.go`). An administrator cannot add a type their teams need, such as "Change request" or "Incident", or stop offering one.

This gives administrators a library of issue types on the Admin page. Built-in types stay as they are, since code finds them by name (the service desk, bootstrap, the demo).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A migration adds `builtin` (every existing type true) and `retired_at` to `issue_type`, and a check that the icon is one the web knows (`typeIcons` in `features/issues/badges.tsx`, with a few new glyphs).
- [ ] The database refuses renaming a built-in type, changing its level, retiring it or deleting it.
- [ ] `GET /issue-types` says whether each type is built in or retired, and lists retired ones only with `?retired=true`.
- [ ] Installation administrators `POST /issue-types`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /issue-types/{typeID}`, and `POST /issue-types/{typeID}/retire` and `/reinstate`. Each writes an audit entry. A custom type may sit at any hierarchy level.
- [ ] Deleting a type that issues use is refused with a sentence that says to retire it instead.
- [ ] `/admin/issue-types` lists the types with Built-in and Retired tags, and creates, edits, retires, reinstates and deletes them.
- [ ] `make openapi` regenerated.

## Tests

Go integration (`test/issue_types_test.go`, parallel, names from `h.name`): create, edit, retire, reinstate and delete a type; a member is refused with 403. Through SQL: renaming a built-in, an unknown icon and deleting a type in use are refused.

Vitest: the page lists, tags and edits types, and shows the refusal sentence.

Browser (e2e): `issue-types.mjs` creates a type with `uniqueName`, edits, retires and deletes it. The edit and retire requests are added to the installation-wide list in `e2e/runner.mjs`.

## Depends on

- #462

issues.title: Each project allows its own issue types
issues.body:
Every project can use every issue type. A project that only tracks bugs and tasks still offers epics and stories, and a custom type from the library would reach every project at once. Each project should keep its own set of allowed types, chosen by its administrators.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A migration adds `project_issue_type(project_id, issue_type_id, position)`, filled with every type for every existing project, so nothing changes for them.
- [ ] An issue's and a request type's `(project_id, issue_type_id)` must be in that set, enforced by a foreign key. It refuses a type the project does not allow, a move into a project that lacks the type, and taking a type away while issues still use it. Deleting a project still removes everything.
- [ ] The database refuses a retired type on a new issue, on a type change and when it is added to a project, and keeps at least one standard (level 0) type in every project.
- [ ] A new project allows every built-in type that is not retired.
- [ ] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/issue-types` for the project's readers, and `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/issue-types` with `typeIds` in order for its administrators.
- [ ] Every way of setting a type checks the set first and refuses with a sentence that says what to do: creating (the default becomes the first allowed standard type), CSV import (naming the row), changing type, moving one issue, a subtree or in bulk ("PROJ does not use Bug; ask its administrator to allow it or change the type first."), the hierarchy, automation and the service desk.
- [ ] Search, reports, field layouts and workflow schemes keep listing every type.
- [ ] `make openapi` regenerated.

## Tests

Go integration: one test per way of setting a type above, each refused for a type the project does not allow and accepted once it is allowed. Through SQL: an issue with a type outside the set, a retired type, and removing a project's last standard type are refused, and deleting a project still cascades.

## Depends on

- #464

issues.title: Pickers offer only the project's issue types
issues.body:
With each project allowing its own issue types, the pickers in the web still offer the whole library (`useIssueTypes`). Its administrators also need a place to choose the types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An "Issue types" tab in the project's Settings: a checklist of the library in the project's order. A type that issues still use cannot be unticked, and the page says why.
- [ ] `useProjectIssueTypes(projectKey)` replaces the library in the create dialog, the type picker, the hierarchy, the plan's timeline, the import's words card and the request-type form of the service desk.
- [ ] Moving an issue into a project that does not allow its type shows the server's sentence.
- [ ] Strings in English and German.

## Tests

Vitest: each of these components offers only the project's types, and the tab keeps a type in use ticked.

Browser (e2e): narrow a project to Task and Bug. Creating and changing type offer only those two, and moving an Epic into the project is refused with the sentence.

## Depends on

- #463
- #465

issues.title: Administrators store project templates
issues.body:
Project templates are code (`backend/internal/template/template.go`, "Templates are code, not rows"). An administrator cannot keep a template for how their teams work, with their workflow scheme, features and issue types.

The comment's concern is that an editable template would need every project made from it to say which version it meant. That does not arise if a template is applied once: the project copies what it needs and never refers back, so editing or archiving a template changes no project. Built-ins stay code; stored templates sit beside them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A migration adds `project_template` (name unique regardless of case, description, kind, board type, planning method, features, an optional workflow scheme, desk, archived, who made it) and `project_template_issue_type`. The database refuses a desk template that is not a service project, a template without a standard type that is not retired, and deleting a scheme a template uses.
- [ ] Built-in templates name their issue types (none named means every built-in type, as today).
- [ ] `GET /project-templates` lists the built-ins, then the stored templates by name, each saying whether it is built in, its scheme and its types. A stored template's key is its id.
- [ ] Installation administrators `POST /project-templates` (with `from` to duplicate a built-in or stored one), `PATCH /project-templates/{id}`, and `POST .../archive` and `.../restore`. Archived templates are listed with `?archived=true`.
- [ ] Creating a project from a stored template gives it the template's kind, board, planning method, features, scheme and issue types, and sets up the desk when asked. An archived template is refused.
- [ ] The doc comment in `template/template.go` and `docs/decisions.md` say that a template is applied once and never referred back to.
- [ ] `make openapi` regenerated.

## Tests

Go integration (`template_test.go`): a project made from a stored template gets exactly its types, scheme and features. Editing or archiving the template changes no project made from it. An archived template is refused. A member is refused with 403. Duplicating Scrum copies its workflow and features. Through SQL: the three refusals above.

## Depends on

- #465

issues.title: Make and edit project templates on the Admin page
issues.body:
Stored project templates need a place on the Admin page where administrators make and keep them, and the "New project" form needs to offer them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/admin/project-templates` shows the built-in templates with "Duplicate", and the stored ones with "Edit", "Archive" and "Restore".
- [ ] The editor sets name, description, kind, board, planning method, features, a workflow scheme from the library and the issue types from the library in order, and the desk when the kind is service.
- [ ] The template chooser in "New project" shows the stored templates after the built-ins, and its summary names the scheme and the types. Archived templates are not offered.
- [ ] Strings in English and German.

## Tests

Vitest: the editor sends what was chosen and shows refusals. `TemplateChooser.test.tsx` shows stored templates after the built-ins.

Browser (e2e, `templates.mjs`): duplicate Scrum under a `uniqueName`, narrow its types, make a project from it and check its type picker, then archive the template and see it leave the chooser.

issues.title: feat(auth): sign-in page as Stator's and Exciter's
issues.body:
The three tools show one sign-in page, set out in [docs/administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#the-sign-in-page) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75), and Stator's and Exciter's is the reference (`web/src/features/auth/LoginPage.tsx` in either). Armature's `/login` puts the password form first and the single sign-on button under it. A person the provider knew but nobody let in yet sees an error.

## Done when
- `/login` shows, in this order:
  - the logo, "Armature", "Sign in" and "Sign in through your identity provider.";
  - a card with the primary button "Sign in with SSO";
  - a second card for the password, with a secondary button, a heading and hint that say who signs in that way here, and the link for a forgotten password.
- `not_a_member` shows as a waiting notice, a status titled "Your request is waiting", not as an error banner.
- The other single sign-on failures keep a sentence each that says what to do, worded as Stator's and Exciter's: expired, not set up, no email, unverified email, switched off, refused, unreachable, anything else.
- The way to sign up, or to ask to be invited, stays below the cards where it is offered. The confirmation after a password reset stays.
- The browser tests and the e2e contract (`docs/design/07-e2e-contract.md`) follow the new page. `data-action="single-sign-on"` keeps working or is renamed in both.

issues.title: feat(access): a built-in Everyone group
issues.body:
The suite's access model ([docs/administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#access) in Dynamo, praetorianer777/Dynamo#75) lets a grant reach every member through a built-in Everyone group. Stator and Exciter already grant to "everyone" and will move to that group. Armature has no such group, so something meant for all members has to be granted to each person, or to a group someone keeps up by hand.

## Done when
- A built-in group Everyone holds every member of the installation, and not portal customers. It cannot be deleted, renamed or edited by hand.
- A grant may name it like any other group. Granting it global administration is refused, as Stator and Exciter refuse "everyone" as administrator.
- The Groups and Roles tabs show it first.
- `docs/design/05-pages.md` describes Access as it is now: under Admin, not "Settings / Access".

issues.title: feat(projects): settings open to every member, sections in the suite's order
issues.body:
Armature's project settings are the reference for the suite's layout. What differs from the standard is who may open them and the order of the sections.

The standard is [administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#settings-of-a-project-or-space) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Where it differs from what follows, the standard wins.

## Done when
- Every project member may open the settings and sees them read-only; sections only administrators use are hidden. The sidebar's "Settings" entry shows for every member.
- Sections in the standard's order: General, Work items (Issue types, Fields, Issue view), Workflow (Workflows), Integrations (Components, Repositories, Automation), Import and export (Import), with archive and delete at the foot of General.
- Each moved tab's old address redirects to its section.
- `docs/design/04-shell-navigation.md` describes the project settings as they are, not the folded "Project Admin" group.

issues.title: feat(ui): follow the suite's shell and feedback
issues.body:
Armature's shell and feedback are mostly the reference, but some of it differs from Stator and Exciter, and from Armature's own rules.

The standard is [look-and-feel.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/look-and-feel.md) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Where it differs from what follows, the standard wins.

## Done when
- **Errors inside the shell**: a page that is not there, or fails, stays inside the shell with its sidebar, as Stator's and Exciter's `routes/root.tsx`; not bare centred text.
- **Loading**: skeletons where a page loads, and no "Loading" string, as `docs/design/06-feedback-rules.md` already says.
- **Breadcrumbs** are derived from the places and drawn in the sticky strip, as Exciter's `Crumbs`; pages stop passing a `crumb` node.
- **Rail**: projects are a folder, as in Exciter; the rail's top is a `div` inside the navigation.
- **Account menu** opens to the right of the rail, and signing out goes to the sign-in page however it ends (`onSettled`).
- **Palette hint** is translated and says Cmd on a Mac, not a hard-coded `Ctrl K` (`features/shell/Sidebar.tsx`).
- **Badges** use the shared `Count` style, accent-subtle and capped at 99+, instead of `UnreadBadge`.
- **Notifications**: `/inbox` becomes the "Notifications" page, with the old address redirecting.
- **Menus** are drawn inside their trigger's landmark.
- `docs/design/04-shell-navigation.md` describes the shell as it is: no sidebar foot, the drawer below 768 px.

issues.title: feat(themes): follow Stator's or Exciter's theme
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter can follow Armature's theme (a theme source of "armature"), but Armature cannot follow theirs, which the suite's standard asks for (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75, `docs/look-and-feel.md`, "Each tool can follow a partner's theme"). #473 left it out: Armature is only an OAuth provider to its partners today, so following them needs it to become their API client.

## Done when
- A person can pick Stator's or Exciter's theme as theirs in Armature, and it follows the partner's changes.
- Armature reads it with the person's own partner token, cached, and falls back to the built-in theme when the partner is unreachable.
- The integration tests use fake partners; the suite's run checks it against the real ones.

issues.title: The suite demo brings Rotor and every issue, with its milestones as GitHub has them
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Armature with Stator, Exciter and Rotor, I want the suite demo to hold every issue of all four tools with their milestones as they are on GitHub, so that the demo shows the suite's real, current work and the other tools' demos link to it.

Extends the suite demo of #300.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Rotor:** the suite demo makes a fourth project, `ROT`, from Cloudster1/Rotor, under the same rules as `ARM`, `EXC` and `STA` (`ROT-42` is Rotor's issue 42, "Depends on" blocks across all four).
- [ ] **Every issue:** the snapshot is taken again, so it holds every issue of the four repositories, pull requests left out.
- [ ] **Milestones as on GitHub:** each project gets every milestone of its repository, also one without issues, with its description and due date; a closed milestone is closed. Today a milestone is made only from an issue's milestone title.
- [ ] **Labels as on GitHub:** a label keeps its colour, nearest of Armature's colours.
- [ ] **Copy:** the Installation card, README and CHANGELOG name all four tools.
- [ ] An installation that already has the three-project demo can add `ROT` without a key clash, or says why not.

## Tests

- Go unit: the snapshot's milestones (open, closed, empty, with and without a due date) and label colours become the plan.
- Integration: the demo makes four projects; a closed milestone is closed with its issues; a "Depends on" into `ROT` is a blocking link.
- vitest and Playwright: the card lists four tools.

## Implementation

- `deploy/demo-snapshot.sh`: the line `rotor Cloudster1/Rotor ROT Rotor`, and the milestones and labels of each repository from `gh api`.
- `backend/internal/demo/suite.go`: `SuiteKeys` gains `ROT`; milestones and labels come from the snapshot's lists rather than the issues.
